title: Mandatory Conditor bootstrap never recorded, yet all later mission work proceeded
description: AGENT-MISSION step 0 makes Conditor bootstrap mandatory and says to finish it before any other mission work, with evidence recorded in requirements/conditor-installation-report.md. That file is absent at baseline 777a70d. So is requirements/echelon-capability-matrix.md (step 1). Waves 1-5, governance, administration, REQ-X-018..084 and this repository's other requirement sets were all produced after step 0. Wave 2 item 5 instead says analysis 'may continue without falsely claiming installation', which reverses the mission's ordering without a recorded owner waiver.
impact: The governing mission instruction has been silently overridden. No artifact can show it was produced under the mandated EF toolchain. The 'EF capability experiment' evidence (CHARTER principle 7) lacks its required baseline.
proposed_resolution: The owner records one of two decisions: (a) a dated waiver allowing requirements-only work before bootstrap, scoped and justified, with step 0 amended; or (b) a bootstrap that is executed and reported. Until then, mark every post-mission artifact 'produced without Conditor bootstrap' and do not count it toward the gate.

title: No requirements-gate PASS/FAIL record; gate criteria have no owner or measurable thresholds
description: AGENT-MISSION step 10 requires an explicit PASS/FAIL for the requirements gate. No such record exists. The validation program's readiness report classifies specification coherence (C/U/I/X/B/N) and proposes its own gates TR-1..TR-6, which are not the CHARTER gate. The CHARTER gate criteria ('all domains have documented coverage', 'contradictions are adjudicated') name no decision owner, denominator, evidence artifact or threshold.
impact: Nobody can tell whether detailed architecture is authorized. Unsupported PASS-by-default is the failure the mission forbids.
proposed_resolution: Publish a gate record that states the current status (FAIL), has one row per CHARTER criterion (owner, measure, denominator, evidence path, status), and names the gate approver. Add the TR-1..TR-6 gates as criteria or reconcile them explicitly. See UNB-RCN-ENT-001.

title: No MVP or release boundary: the requirement set targets the whole DAF industry at once
description: EXPANSION roadmap tracks R1 to R8 cover every enterprise function. REQ-X-056 requires every material competitive capability to map to a requirement. Seven landscape gaps are P0 (nonprofit portal, complex gifts, regulatory reporting, migration, advisor/CRM/SMA, embedded checkout, legal operating models), and adjacencies follow (workplace, foundations/trusts, campaigns). The CHARTER mission is a synthetic reference enterprise, and PRINCIPLES forbids real sponsor operations. UNB-COM-004 separates the reference enterprise from the commercial model. Nothing defines which capabilities a first validated release needs, or what is deferred or out of scope.
impact: The requirement set cannot be finished or gated, and parity chasing will keep expanding scope. Effort goes to P2 adjacencies before the core money path (contribution to grant to payment to close) is fully specified.
proposed_resolution: Define a release-1 boundary as an outcome slice: one legal sponsor, cash and public-securities contributions, domestic grants to eligible public charities, multi-participant funds, succession, closure, statements, Schedule D data. Classify every other REQ-X/UNB family as in, deferred or excluded, with an owner, and make REQ-X-056 parity a backlog input, not a requirement. See UNB-RCN-ENT-002.

title: 'Operating model' has three incompatible meanings, and the CHARTER-mandated three-model comparison never happened
description: CHARTER requires comparing three autonomy/organization models (radically autonomous; human-governed AI orchestration; API-first networked philanthropy) on identical scenarios, and makes that comparison a gate criterion. UNB-COM-001 compares business models A/B/C/D/Dc. REQ-X-057 and the one-system invariant use 'operating models' to mean commercial service channels (sponsor SaaS, outsourced admin, turnkey, embedded, digital). No Unbound artifact compares the CHARTER's three models, and REQ-X-057 fixes the architecture first.
impact: The gate criterion 'operating models are compared on common criteria' cannot be evaluated. Readers will treat REQ-X-057 as having met the CHARTER obligation when it has not.
proposed_resolution: Adopt three distinct terms: autonomy model (CHARTER), sponsor business model (UNB-COM), service/channel model (REQ-X-057). The owner then either runs the CHARTER comparison as configurations inside the one system or amends CHARTER principle 4. See RCC-ENT-002.

title: Program naming collision: Unbound (repo/brand) vs 'Strata' (owner's program name and an EF persistence component)
description: UNB-EXP-002 requires the public identity to be branded 'Unbound'. The owner refers to the program as 'Strata'. In the repository, 'Strata' names a mandatory persistence component (UNB-TEC-STRATA-001). The verified kemiller2002/strata is a pilot declarative PostgreSQL schema management tool. A requirement reading 'Strata SHALL ...' is therefore ambiguous between the program and the component.
impact: Stakeholders may misread program-level obligations as persistence-component obligations, or the reverse. Brand requirements may diverge from how the owner names the product.
proposed_resolution: Owner decision: choose the program name, and reserve 'Strata' only for the EF schema-management component. Add a glossary entry and amend UNB-EXP-002 if the brand changes. Never use a bare 'Strata' to mean the program.

title: Unbound-branded public identity contradicts the white-label, multi-sponsor platform and mandatory legal-sponsor disclosure
description: UNB-EXP-002 makes the public identity 'Unbound', which implies Unbound is the donor-facing sponsor brand (model B). REQ-X-057 and the one-system invariant describe white-label, multi-sponsor channels, and INV-18 requires the legally responsible sponsoring charity to be disclosed in every channel. The requirements never say whether 'Unbound' is the sponsor, the platform, or the reference-enterprise name, and UNB-COM-004 says this should not be decided yet.
impact: A donor could be misled about which charity legally holds the assets, which is the INV-18 harm. Brand, disclosure and acknowledgment wording (CTL-020) cannot be specified.
proposed_resolution: Split the brand into platform name, reference-sponsor name (synthetic) and partner sponsor brand. Make the legal-sponsor disclosure a non-configurable element. See RCC-ENT-001.

evidence: requirements/the wave 2 conversion file.md:35;requirements/the wave 2 conversion file.md:37;research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/19-questions/PROPOSED-CANONICAL-REQUIREMENTS-AND-ACCEPTANCE-2026-11-22.md:614;research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/19-questions/CROSS-WORKFLOW-FINANCIAL-AUTHORITY-AND-IRREVERSIBILITY-INVARIANTS-2026-11-23.md:14;research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/19-questions/END-TO-END-DAF-ENTERPRISE-WORKFLOW-COMPLETENESS-AUDIT-2026-11-23.md:29;requirements/administration/DAF-ADMINISTRATION-AND-SPONSOR-OPERATIONS.md:61;requirements/MULTI-PARTICIPANT-AND-SUCCESSOR-ACCOUNTS.md:75
title: Workflow IDs WF-nn have at least four incompatible namespaces
description: Bare WF-nn has four meanings. UNB-WF-001..024 map the landscape WF-01..24 (WF-13 = donor death, WF-17 = liquidity shock). REQ-X-078's end-to-end audit uses WF-01..18 (WF-13 = month-end close, WF-17 = migration). Administration uses WF-01..16 (WF-10 = dormancy, WF-11 = closure). The research program uses CW-01..38. The INV-01..18 table cites bare WF-nn in the REQ-X-078 sense, while MULTI-PARTICIPANT traceability cites UNB-WF-013 in the landscape sense.
impact: Traceability and the REQ-X-082 static checker resolve references to the wrong workflow. Example: INV-07 (migration fencing) appears to govern liquidity shocks.
proposed_resolution: Introduce qualified namespaces (LS-WF, E2E-WF, ADM-WF, CW) with a crosswalk, and reject bare WF-nn in new text. See UNB-RCN-ENT-003.

title: Duplicate: UNB-GAP-001..009 defined twice with different content; GAP-001 has four meanings
description: Two files define UNB-GAP-001..009 with different meanings. In Wave 1 they are validation blockers (shadow replay, break costs, API rights...). In the Enterprise Gap Register they are reconciliation and grant requirements. Bare GAP-001..020 (landscape gap register) and GAP-001/034 (economics shadow replay in the readiness report) add more meanings.
impact: Any cross-reference to UNB-GAP-00n or GAP-00n is ambiguous. Coverage counts double-count or drop items.
proposed_resolution: Renumber Wave 1 items as UNB-VBLK-001..009 (validation blockers). Prefix landscape gaps LSGAP-001..020. Keep UNB-GAP-001..034 for the Enterprise Gap Register. Publish a redirect table.

title: Control crosswalks omit the BASELINE, participant, workflow, cross-domain and REQ-X requirement families
description: The two requirement-to-control crosswalks map UNB-SUCC (67 rows) but no requirement from UNB-ENT, UNB-LEG, UNB-DON, UNB-GRT, UNB-AST, UNB-FIN, UNB-ADV, UNB-AIO, UNB-OPS, UNB-EXP, UNB-VAL, UNB-PART, UNB-WF, UNB-GAP, UNB-LS, UNB-HYP, UNB-XSC, UNB-REM, UNB-TRACE or REQ-X. UNB-LEG-002 (sponsor legal control), the core legal invariant, has no mapped control.
impact: The CHARTER gate requirement that legal assertions have traceable controls cannot be met. Control coverage figures overstate completeness for the enterprise domain.
proposed_resolution: Extend the crosswalk to every requirement family, with gap_or_review rows where no control exists. Make 'no control mapped' a gate-blocking status for P0 legal and financial requirements.

title: Most enterprise-domain 'requirements' lack the CHARTER record fields, and many are backlog topics rather than requirements
description: CHARTER makes about 15 attributes mandatory on every requirement, including type, source, owner, measurable acceptance and scenarios. In scope, 160 requirements are inventoried. UNB-LS (0/17), UNB-GAP (0/34), UNB-REM (0/15) and UNB-HYP (0/10) contain no RFC 2119 keyword. None of the 160 is referenced by a test artifact. UNB-GAP and UNB-REM items are phrased 'Define X' or 'Specify Y', which makes them work items. REQ-X-058..064 consist only of 'Specify the full operating workflow in <file>' plus a shared template paragraph.
impact: None of these can be verified, so the gate cannot pass on coverage claims.
proposed_resolution: Reclassify UNB-GAP, UNB-REM and UNB-LS items as backlog epics or outcomes with status 'not a requirement'. Require all CHARTER record fields before any item takes the status 'candidate requirement'. Replace pointer-only REQ-X items with clause-level requirements, using the refinements in this audit as the pattern.

title: Duplicate: succession and donor-death rules are specified in eight places without a canonical owner
description: Donor death and succession appear in UNB-SUCC-001..014, UNB-WF-013, UNB-GAP-015, REQ-X-008, REQ-X-068 (plus its detail file), ADM-007/ADM-022, E2E WF-18 and UNB-XSC-004. The rules diverge: suspension timing differs (UNB-SUCC-008 at activation; the landscape design and ADM-022 at verified evidence), and pending-grant treatment differs (REQ-X-008 does not cancel; FM-05 cancels or suspends).
impact: Implementers choose whichever text they find first, and authority over pending grants after a death becomes inconsistent.
proposed_resolution: Make UNB-SUCC the canonical family. Mark the others 'refined-by UNB-SUCC' and remove normative text from them. Adopt RR-UNB-SUCC-008-r1 and RR-REQ-X-008-r1.

title: Duplicate: portability, transfer and migration requirements overlap and conflate three different processes
description: Seven items cover overlapping portability and migration ground. Together they mix three different processes: (1) a donor-initiated transfer of one fund to another sponsor, legally a sponsor distribution; (2) an institution migrating its platform with the sponsor unchanged (REQ-X-061); and (3) a partner or sponsor exiting with data handover (UNB-GAP-025/028).
impact: Requirements written for institutional migration (cutover fencing, parallel run) get applied to single-fund transfers, and donor-level portability falls between them.
proposed_resolution: Split into three canonical requirements: UNB-WF-014 (fund outbound transfer), REQ-X-061 (platform migration) and sponsor/partner exit. Link the others as refined-by.

title: Duplicate: donor and advisor identity onboarding specified five times with different scopes
description: Identity proofing and onboarding appear in UNB-PART-007, UNB-GAP-014, REQ-X-072, UNB-WF-012 and ADM-009. None states which identity regime applies (see RCF-ENT-014). ADM-009 adds 'source of funds', which appears nowhere else.
impact: Diligence obligations will be inconsistent across channels.
proposed_resolution: Make REQ-X-072 plus UNB-PART-007 canonical, with the regime taxonomy in UNB-RCN-ENT-014.

title: KYC is used as a fund-opening gate without determining whether it is law, contract or sponsor policy
description: E2E WF-02's lifecycle (Invitation > IdentityPending > EligibilityValidated...) has a 'Failed KYC' exception. ADM-009 requires identity, entity status and source-of-funds verification. EXPANSION says 'KYC/identity where applicable'. The source AML rows are classified risk_control 'no / conditional', and Wave 5 warns that negative applicability claims need entity facts. Whether a Bank Secrecy Act customer-identification program applies to a 501(c)(3) sponsoring organization is unresolved. Sponsors are generally not banks, but a custodian, broker or payment provider may impose identification by contract. Sanctions screening (OFAC) is a separate regime. Identity proofing for account security is a third, and source-of-funds diligence (gift-acceptance policy) a fourth. The requirements merge all four into 'KYC'.
impact: Two failure modes: unnecessary collection of personal data into an append-only store (conflicts with UNB-DATA-007 minimization), or a false claim of regulatory compliance. Neither path defines what happens when identity fails after an irrevocable contribution has arrived.
proposed_resolution: Needs counsel. Replace 'KYC' with four separately classified obligations, each with an authority type (statute/regulation, contract, sponsor policy, risk control) and an owner. Define failure outcomes per regime, including a contribution already received. See RR-UNB-PART-007-r1 and UNB-RCN-ENT-014.

title: REQ-X-008 adopts as normative the answer to open owner decision OD-03, and is ambiguous for multi-participant funds
description: OD-03 (sponsor board + GC) is open and blocks GR-8/CW-11. REQ-X-008 nonetheless states 'Donor death does not automatically cancel valid sponsor-approved unpaid grants', which is the program's recommended option. Separately, 'future instructions suspend until successor authority verified' does not say whose instructions. Under UNB-PART-001 a fund may have five independent advisors, and the death of one should not suspend the surviving advisors' own scoped rights.
impact: Approved grants may be paid, or blocked, without the sponsor's governing decision. Surviving co-advisors could be locked out unnecessarily, or the deceased's delegated rights could continue.
proposed_resolution: Make the pending-grant disposition a sponsor policy parameter, death_pending_grant_policy in {complete, hold_for_review, cancel}, with no default until OD-03 is answered. Scope suspension to rights that derive from the deceased party. See RR-REQ-X-008-r1 and RCC-ENT-003. OD-03, TVF-018 and TVC-030 remain open; the requirements have not resolved them.

title: Former advisory authority stays live from verified death until succession activation
description: UNB-SUCC-008 suspends or revokes former advisory authority only as part of 'succession activation'. Activation waits for sponsor approval and may be held for disputes (UNB-SUCC-007). In the meantime, the deceased donor's credentials, sessions, delegated AI-agent principals (UNB-WF-011) and derived privileges stay usable. The landscape design suspends all donor-derived privileges immediately on verification. UNB-SUCC-006 forbids activating anything on an unverified allegation, but says nothing about protective holds on allegation.
impact: Family members or attackers holding the deceased's credentials can submit recommendations or change contacts during the gap. That raises unauthorized-recommendation and account-takeover risk on a fund whose authority is in transition.
proposed_resolution: Separate the three steps: protective hold on any notice (new recommendations only), suspension on verified death, and successor activation later. See RR-UNB-SUCC-008-r1 and UNB-RCN-ENT-004. TVF-187 and TVF-202 (unauthenticated-notice scope) remain open.

title: Fractional successor allocations lack a rounding, valuation-date, unit and residual rule, so 'reconcile exactly' cannot be tested
description: UNB-SUCC-004 allows percentage or amount allocations across several successor accounts and requires exact reconciliation, but defines none of: valuation timestamp; currency versus unit basis; rounding and residual-cent assignment; treatment of reservations, accrued fees and open grants; in-kind versus liquidated allocation of illiquid positions; or the destination of trailing receipts and returns after the split (OD-11, TVF-128).
impact: Different implementations will produce different successor balances from the same plan. Odd-cent residuals and NAV movement between decision and posting create unexplained differences.
proposed_resolution: Adopt the deterministic allocation rule in RR-UNB-SUCC-004-r1. Make the valuation point and residual rule explicit sponsor parameters with a CFO owner.

title: No rule says whether a successor account at another sponsor or program is an internal allocation or a distribution
description: MULTI-PARTICIPANT leaves open the legal distinction between an internal successor-account allocation and a transfer to another sponsoring organization. UNB-SUCC-014 still mentions cross-sponsor cases, and PARTNER-SEGREGATION scenario 12 assumes a successor account can sit in a different partner channel under the same sponsor. Inbound transfers have no classification (TVF-121).
impact: Cross-sponsor successor creation might be booked as an internal allocation when it is legally a grant to another charity, which would misstate grants and Schedule D.
proposed_resolution: Needs counsel. Allow internal allocations only within the same legal sponsor entity. Route any other destination through UNB-WF-014 as a sponsor distribution.

title: Dormancy is a one-line requirement framed as 'unclaimed accounts', which confuses sponsor-owned balances with escheat
description: UNB-WF-015 says only 'follow approved notice, successor and charitable-default policies'. ADM-024 is titled 'Dormancy and unclaimed accounts'. Under UNB-LEG-002 a DAF balance is a sponsor-owned charitable asset. Whether state unclaimed-property law reaches a fund balance (as opposed to an uncashed grant check, CTL-044) needs counsel and must not be presumed. Inactivity thresholds are sponsor program policy, not statute. No Unbound state machine, threshold parameter, outreach rule or reactivation path exists. The landscape (WF-15) provides a candidate Active > Quiet > Inactive > Unresponsive > CharitableDefault flow and warns that reminders must not steer toward recipients in which the sponsor has a financial interest.
impact: Charitable-default distributions are irreversible and override donor expectations. Undefined policy invites inconsistent, disputable distributions and possibly mistaken escheat filings.
proposed_resolution: See UNB-RCN-ENT-005: a sponsor-parameterized dormancy lifecycle, with escheat applicability limited to payment instruments pending counsel.

title: REQ-X-078's '18 enterprise workflows' omit fund closure, dormancy, outbound and inbound transfer, fund split/merge and sponsor succession
description: REQ-X-078 treats WF-01..18 as the end-to-end completeness baseline. It has no workflow for donor-requested or policy-triggered fund closure, dormancy, donor-initiated outbound transfer to another sponsor, inbound transfer, fund split or merge outside succession, or sponsoring-organization merger and dissolution (TVF-130). The landscape WF-14/15 and administration WF-10/11 cover some of these but are not traced. EXPANSION completeness check 1 requires all 24 landscape workflows to map.
impact: A completeness claim based on 18 workflows hides lifecycle-ending money movements, which are where trailing receipts, uncashed checks and residual-balance errors concentrate.
proposed_resolution: Add E2E workflows for closure, dormancy, outbound transfer, inbound transfer, split/merge and sponsor succession, each to the REQ-X-078 transition standard. See UNB-RCN-ENT-005..008.

title: Outbound sponsor-to-sponsor transfer has no specified treatment
description: UNB-WF-014 is one sentence. Nothing specifies: whether the transfer is processed as a grant to the receiving sponsor (the landscape claims it is 'legally a grant', a source claim to verify); receiving-sponsor eligibility; the sponsor's discretion to decline; cash versus in-kind; partial versus full transfer; fund-closure linkage; a DAF-to-DAF purpose tag (the industry report says such transfers are 10-18% of national sponsors' grant dollars and distort reported payout); or the history package. No reviewed sponsor publishes an outbound policy.
impact: Transfers could bypass grant eligibility controls or misstate grant and payout reporting. Donors lose history.
proposed_resolution: Needs counsel on classification. See RR-UNB-WF-014-r1 and UNB-RCN-ENT-007.

title: Fund closure has no state machine or trigger catalogue in the UNB requirement families
description: Closure exists only as ADM-025, ADM WF-11, SIM-018 and the 'Suspended/Closed' tail of E2E WF-02. The UNB families do not define closure triggers (donor request, zero balance after final grant, dormancy default, completed succession split, outbound transfer, sponsor exit), final fee proration, reservation and attempt terminality (TVF-129/199), trailing receipts (OD-11 open), reopening, or the retention clock.
impact: Funds may close with live obligations, or never reach a closed state because issued checks can stay outstanding for years.
proposed_resolution: See UNB-RCN-ENT-006. TVF-021/108/182/190/199 remain open.

title: Paying a donor's personal investment advisor from fund assets is treated as a fee-disclosure topic, not a legal-applicability gate
description: REQ-X-062 requires fee waterfall and related-party compensation records 'with sponsor approvals and donor-facing disclosures', and CTL-025 enforces an advisor fee cap. Neither routes the arrangement to counsel. The DAF provisions of the Internal Revenue Code address excess-benefit transactions involving donors, donor advisors and certain investment advisors to sponsoring organizations (statute; exact subsection applicability to be verified). The 2023 proposed §4966 regulations, still proposed per the landscape (proposed regulation, not binding), address when a personal investment advisor is treated as a donor advisor. TVF-175 covers grants that pay a donor or advisor, not advisory fees paid from fund assets.
impact: An advisor-managed fund program could create excess-benefit exposure for the sponsor and managers if fee arrangements are configured as a commercial setting.
proposed_resolution: Needs counsel. Do not activate fees paid from fund assets to any party with advisory privileges or a personal advisory relationship with the donor until a counsel-approved rule exists. Track the proposed regulations as a watch item with an effective-date trigger. See UNB-RCN-ENT-015.

title: 'Advisor' is overloaded: donor advisor, professional/investment advisor and successor advisor
description: CHARTER defines UNB-ADV as 'advisor relationships, delegated authority, consent, integrations', meaning professional or wealth advisors. UNB-ADV-001 ('Advisors SHALL operate only within explicit, revocable, scoped delegated permissions') reads equally as donor advisors. UNB-PART-003 distinguishes original, additional, professional and successor advisors, but BASELINE does not. The tax law uses 'donor advisor' as a defined term (statute; counsel to confirm the definition's reach).
impact: Permission and legal-status rules for wealth managers could be applied to donor advisors, or the reverse.
proposed_resolution: Adopt a glossary: 'advisory-privilege holder' (donor-side), 'professional advisor' (wealth/investment), 'successor advisor'. Refine UNB-ADV-001 (RR-UNB-ADV-001-r1).

title: Households and joint donors have no rules for contributor of record, separation or divorce, or household privacy
description: ADM-008 treats a household as a display grouping. The UNB-PART family has no household concept, although EXPANSION R1 lists households. Nothing determines: the contributor of record (acknowledgment recipient) for gifts from joint accounts or third-party payers; how a co-donor fund is divided on divorce or a family split outside succession (REQ-X-068 lists 'divorce' only as a test case); or what household members may see of each other's contributions.
impact: Acknowledgments could go to the wrong person, a disputed split could be handled ad hoc, and household views could leak private contribution data.
proposed_resolution: See UNB-RCN-ENT-008 and UNB-RCN-ENT-009. Acknowledgment identity needs CPA and counsel input.

title: Role taxonomy omits legal representatives (POA agent, guardian, executor, trustee, entity signatory)
description: UNB-SUCC-007 mentions 'lawful representative authority' and ADM-005 mentions a representative, but UNB-PART-003's enumerated roles exclude agents under power of attorney, guardians or conservators, personal representatives or executors, trustees of trust donors, and authorized signatories of entity donors.
impact: Incapacity and estate cases will be handled with sponsor-staff overrides instead of scoped, evidenced roles.
proposed_resolution: Extend the UNB-PART-003 role catalogue with representative roles. Each carries evidence type, scope, expiry and a sponsor-policy flag (see RR-UNB-PART-003-r1).

title: Migration imports standing data (payees, successors, advisors) without required provenance or verification state, and has no rollback boundary
description: REQ-X-061 lists import contracts and the stage-to-cutover sequence. It does not require imported payee, bank, successor or advisor records to carry source provenance, a verification status and an 'imported-unverified' flag that blocks payment until verified. The E2E audit records the hard rollback boundary after the first live posting as unresolved.
impact: Migration is the largest write to payment-destination data, so a corrupted or malicious legacy file could redirect grants. A failed cutover after live postings has no defined compensation.
proposed_resolution: TVF-208, TVF-217 and TVF-244 remain open and REQ-X-061 has not resolved them. Adopt RR-REQ-X-061-r1.

title: Donor-level data portability is a hypothesis with no requirement
description: UNB-LS-015 and UNB-HYP-007 name portability. REQ-X-061 is institution-level only. No requirement gives a donor or advisor a self-service, machine-readable export of fund history, grants, contributions and documents, or attaches a history package to an outbound transfer. The industry report says no reviewed sponsor commits to moving grant history.
impact: A differentiating outcome stated in the outcome model is unspecified.
proposed_resolution: See UNB-RCN-ENT-013 (P2).

title: Schedule D DAF reporting and account-type classification are not specified; §6033(k) is not cited in any requirement
description: REQ-X-060 says only 'Form 990 and applicable schedules'. The statute requires a sponsoring organization to report DAF information on its annual return; the form currently collects it on Schedule D Part I (number of funds, contributions, grants, year-end value, plus donor-disclosure questions; verify against the current form and instructions). No requirement defines how these aggregates come from the ledger by legal sponsor and tax year. Also undefined: as-filed snapshots, DAF-to-DAF tagging, exclusion of synthetic or canary items (TVS-469), recognition timing (OD-19 open), and which Unbound account types count as donor-advised funds at all. The industry report shows filers have reclassified micro-donation accounts out of the DAF column, which bears on REQ-X-070 workplace and REQ-X-075 campaign accounts.
impact: Returns could be misstated. If account-type classification is wrong, the excise-tax regimes (§4966/§4967) are applied to the wrong population.
proposed_resolution: Needs CPA and counsel. See UNB-RCN-ENT-011 and UNB-RCN-ENT-012, and RR-REQ-X-060-r1.

title: The legal operating-model matrix omits state charitable-platform and solicitation applicability for the technology-provider role
description: REQ-X-064 maps contractual roles but does not require a per-role, per-state determination of charitable-platform or fundraising-counsel registration. The landscape (a source claim, not verified) reports that California platform rules can reach DAF technology vendors and white-label portals, and that the DAF exclusion names only the sponsor. Source rows REG-046 and REG-053 remain unmapped.
impact: The platform operator could carry unregistered-platform obligations in some states.
proposed_resolution: Needs counsel. Add an applicability row per legal role and state to the SponsorOperatingAgreement responsibility matrix.

title: 'One system, single coordinated deployment' conflicts with the dedicated-infrastructure tenancy profile
description: The one-system invariant requires 'a single coordinated deployment' and rejects any 'second deployable'. PARTNER-SEGREGATION requires dedicated-database and dedicated-infrastructure partner profiles, and UNB-TEN-002 requires them without a business-logic fork. 'One authoritative financial ledger' is also ambiguous once partner ledgers live in separate databases.
impact: Profile C cannot be built without breaking the literal invariant, or the invariant will be used to block a contractual isolation promise.
proposed_resolution: Clarify that 'one' means one codebase, one domain model, one release train and one ledger contract per legal sponsor, deployed as N isolated instances. See RCC-ENT-004.

title: Mandatory component selections were made before the CHARTER-required capability discovery and gate
description: CHARTER requires a dated EF capability matrix before dependencies are selected, and says passing the gate authorizes detailed architecture. Before either exists, EXPANSION and UNB-TEC-STRATA-001 make Strata a mandatory persistence component, and REQ-X-057 fixes Forma, Folio and Limen. The verified Strata is a declarative PostgreSQL schema management tool, so a requirement mandating it for append-only history or replay is unsupported (detailed in the TEC audit).
impact: Requirements rest on unverified component capabilities, so the order the gate depends on is reversed.
proposed_resolution: Move component names into an ADR-gated candidate list (OD-16 recommendation). Keep the outcome requirements (append-only, replay) technology-neutral. TVC-002 and OD-16 are open and extend to Strata.

affected_ids: BASELINE scenario family 'sponsor decision appeal';UNB-GAP-026;UNB-REM-006;E2E WF-16
title: Customer support has no requirement for appeals of sponsor decisions, assisted-channel attribution or support-channel identity assurance
description: BASELINE lists 'sponsor decision appeal' as a mandatory scenario family, but no UNB requirement defines it. UNB-GAP-026 and UNB-REM-006 are topic lists. E2E WF-16 records the appeal and closure-proof gap. TVF-132 (assurance level and attribution of staff-entered recommendations) is open. REQ-X-072 lists 'deepfake support call' only as a test case.
impact: Support staff become an unauthenticated back door to recommendations and contact changes, and donors have no defined route to contest a decision.
proposed_resolution: See UNB-RCN-ENT-016. TVF-132 remains open.

title: The E2E workflow inventory table's column headers do not match its cell contents
description: The header reads 'In-process owner(s) | Requirement anchors | Most important missing transition', but the cells hold the authoritative boundary, exception paths and requirement anchors, in that order.
impact: Automated extraction (REQ-X-082 catalog) and human readers mis-assign fields.
proposed_resolution: Correct the header to 'Authoritative boundary | Exception paths | Requirement anchors'.

title: Failure-mode ID FM-12 means 'duplicate delivery' in the simulation taxonomy and 'account takeover' in the validation program
description: The two failure-mode namespaces collide.
impact: Fault-injection coverage may count the wrong failure class.
proposed_resolution: Prefix the simulation taxonomy (SIM-FM-nn) or crosswalk the two.

title: Succession previews and donor wording risk reading as promises; successor-advisor litigation makes the wording legally sensitive
description: UNB-SUCC-010 requires explaining that a DAF is not personally owned or inherited, and UNB-SUCC-013 requires an allocation simulation preview. The industry report notes pending successor-advisor litigation (Peterson v. WaterStone). Neither requirement requires counsel-approved disclosure text, a statement that successor designations stay subject to sponsor approval at activation, or versioned evidence of what the donor was shown.
impact: A preview or label could later be cited as a sponsor commitment.
proposed_resolution: Needs counsel. Make disclosure text a counsel-approved, versioned Folio artifact. Record the shown version with each SuccessionPlanApproved event, and label previews as non-binding simulations.

title: Tax-fit guidance asserts unspecified 'special 2026 rules' and has the sponsor's fee-earning system compare DAF against direct giving
description: REQ-X-066 requires 'special 2026 rules' without citation, contrary to UNB-LEG-001. It uses holdings and tax lots to compare a DAF with direct giving, which edges toward individualized tax or investment advice (PRINCIPLES forbids tax advice from the reference environment). The comparator is also operated by a party that earns fees when the answer is 'DAF'. The landscape requires a 'direct gift may be better' comparison, but no requirement makes neutrality testable.
impact: Conflicted or unlicensed guidance creates regulatory and reputational exposure.
proposed_resolution: Needs counsel. Cite every tax rule with UNB-LEG-001 metadata. Add a neutrality test (identical inputs produce the direct-gift recommendation where it dominates). Keep individualized output behind a professional-advisor boundary.

title: No normative requirement for DAF contribution acknowledgment content or timing
description: The FIN requirements name 'acknowledgment' only as a lifecycle label (UNB-ACC-006) and a Folio output (UNB-ACC-025). Nothing requires the acknowledgment to contain the statement that the sponsoring organization has exclusive legal control over the contributed assets (IRC 170(f)(18), statute; strict compliance per case law cited in OB-09), the goods-or-services statement and amount or noncash description (IRC 170(f)(8), statute; IRS Pub 1771 guidance), or the date of the completed gift. The content rule exists only as control CTL-020 in a control matrix and as an ontology note, with no requirement that a test can trace to.
impact: Donors can lose deductions for every gift acknowledged with a defective template; the defect would repeat across all sponsors that share a template, and correction after the donor's filing deadline may not cure it.
proposed_resolution: Add UNB-RCN-FIN-001: acknowledgment issuance is a gated command whose content schema is versioned and counsel-approved per sponsor; issuance is blocked when any mandatory element is missing; acknowledgment is linked to the completed-gift event and supports correction and void with preserved originals.

title: UNB-ACC-006 orders acknowledgment before settlement
description: UNB-ACC-006 lists the contribution lifecycle as 'receipt, valuation, restrictions, acceptance, acknowledgment, settlement and disposition'. The transition matrix (TX-03..TX-05) and the daf-landscape recurring-contributions record (D4, CON-REC-09) issue a tax acknowledgment only after a validated, accepted event. REQ-X-009 requires acknowledgment and finality to remain distinct but does not say which gates the other. An implementer following UNB-ACC-006 literally may acknowledge a gift that later returns.
impact: Acknowledgments issued for reversible-rail receipts that later return (ACH R10 window) create donor tax records for gifts that never completed.
proposed_resolution: Make acknowledgment a dependent of a 'completed gift determined' fact (per rail and asset type) plus sponsor acceptance, not a list position; define an acknowledgment void/correction path for subsequently returned receipts.

title: Form 8283 donee signature and Form 8282 disposition reporting are not requirements
description: The only references are UNB-GAP-012 ('support Form 8283/8282 applicability review') and control CTL-022. No requirement makes the donee signature on Form 8283 Section B a tracked task, or links a sale or other disposition of Section B property within three years of receipt to a Form 8282 obligation due within 125 days, with a copy to the donor (IRC 6050L, statute; Form 8282 instructions, IRS guidance; exceptions per instructions). The complex-asset liquidation transition TX-09 has no obligation hook, although DAF sponsors usually sell gifted complex assets quickly.
impact: Without a requirement, disposition-reporting obligations are missed in a predictable, repeated way, with information-return penalties and donor tax exposure.
proposed_resolution: Add UNB-RCN-FIN-002 and UNB-RCN-FIN-003: signing a Form 8283 Section B creates a tracked donee-acknowledgment record; any disposition event on the same asset lot within the statutory window creates a dated 8282 obligation with deadline, owner and filing-receipt evidence. Counsel confirms the exceptions table.

title: Requirements assume the sponsor states a value on noncash acknowledgments
description: UNB-ACC-031 refers to 'donor tax acknowledgment values', and FI-24 defines a 'gift-date valuation for acknowledgment'. IRS guidance (Form 8283 instructions, cited as OB-12) says the donee signature acknowledges receipt, not value, and the 170(f)(8) acknowledgment for property requires a description. Whether, and by what method, a sponsor may print an informational value (for example, for publicly traded securities) is sponsor policy that counsel should approve. For complex assets it can look like the sponsor endorses the donor's appraisal.
impact: Implementers could put sponsor-calculated values on acknowledgments, especially for complex assets, and create liability or conflicts with the donor's qualified appraisal.
proposed_resolution: Restate UNB-ACC-031: acknowledgments carry an asset description; an optional informational value is allowed only for asset classes and methods in a counsel-approved sponsor policy, labelled as not an appraisal; sponsor book value, custody receipt value and sale proceeds stay separate facts.

title: Excess business holdings (IRC 4943 as applied by 4943(e)) are not monitored
description: IRC 4943(e) (statute) applies the excess business holdings rules to DAFs, combining the fund's holdings with those of donors, advisors and related persons, with a disposal period for gifted interests. No FIN requirement asks for business-enterprise holdings to be aggregated across funds and disqualified persons, for permitted-holding limits to be tested at acceptance, or for disposal deadlines to be tracked. CTL-021 mentions an 'excess business holdings test' without a requirement or data model. REQ-X-059 lists private company shares and partnership interests as acceptable asset types.
impact: Accepting closely held business interests without the test can expose the sponsor to the initial and additional excise taxes; the exposure is invisible until a later audit.
proposed_resolution: Add UNB-RCN-FIN-004: maintain business-enterprise identity and ownership for related persons; test at gift acceptance and on every related transaction; track the disposal period with escalation. Counsel defines limits, attribution and exceptions as sponsor-policy parameters; the system must not hard-code them.

title: Advisor compensation paid from DAF assets has no IRC 4958 or proposed-regulation screen
description: The requirements support external RIAs managing DAF assets for fees (UNB-INV-006, UNB-CUST-014, UNB-INV-036, CTL-025), and the daf-landscape evidence confirms the pattern (AEF, Fidelity CIAP, DAFgiving360). Nothing screens whether the advisor is a disqualified person (IRC 4958(f)(1)(F) and (f)(8), statute per OB-06) or a donor-advisor whose compensation from the DAF would be an automatic excess benefit (IRC 4958(c)(2), statute). Nothing tracks the 2023 proposed regulations that would treat personal investment advisers as donor-advisors (proposed, not law, OB-21).
impact: Advisor fees paid from fund assets could be excess-benefit transactions, taxed to the advisor with manager excise exposure. Fee automation would repeat the problem in every period.
proposed_resolution: Add UNB-RCN-FIN-010: advisor engagement requires a recorded relationship classification (donor's personal adviser or not) and a counsel-approved compensation policy before the first fee accrual; status changes of proposed rules are tracked in the regulatory register.

title: No valuation-date or completed-gift-date rules for contributed securities, crypto or complex assets
description: Valuation dates are defined only for pool subscriptions (UNB-INV-023) and NAV runs. Nothing defines, by rail and asset type, when a gift is complete (DTC receipt, certificate delivery, on-chain transfer, deed recording), which price source and timestamp apply, or how the four distinct numbers in FI-24 (acceptance value, custody receipt value, gift-date informational value, sale proceeds) are stored. Crypto trades 24/7, so a valuation point needs an explicit timestamp, time zone and source. IRS Chief Counsel Advice 202302012 (non-precedential guidance) indicates crypto is not exempt from the qualified-appraisal requirement; counsel should confirm. TVF-115 (completed-gift date defined only for DTC) is still open; the requirements did not resolve it.
impact: Inconsistent gift dates and values across acknowledgment, books and statements; crypto may be treated like publicly traded securities and its appraisal requirement missed.
proposed_resolution: Add UNB-RCN-FIN-011 and a completed-gift-date rule table (UNB-RCN-FIN-012), versioned per sponsor policy and counsel-reviewed; store the four values as separate typed facts.

title: Full sponsor ERP scope (AP, AR, budgeting, payroll, fixed assets, consolidation, FX translation) is not needed for DAF administration
description: The binding scope (FULL-ACCOUNTING line 5) requires a 'complete integrated accounting system, not ... an external GL connector', and UNB-ACC-012..016 add AP, purchasing, vendor master, AR, invoicing, budgeting and forecasting, multi-entity consolidation and eliminations, and functional-currency translation; UNB-ACC-004 adds a payroll interface and fixed assets. None of these is needed to administer DAFs. The DAF outcome needs: the fund subledger, the sponsor-level accounts that DAF activity touches (charitable cash, custody, investments, contributions, grants payable, fees), reconciliation, close and fund statements. Sponsors already run operating ERPs. The document itself lists 'whether Unbound is authoritative for sponsor GL' as an open blocker (line 79). Even the daf-landscape financial core puts the DAF financial kernel first and gates everything on it.
impact: Scope roughly doubles accounting build and assurance effort (AP fraud controls, payroll privacy, consolidation) and competes with incumbent ERPs. Sponsor adoption may need the books to live in the sponsor's ERP anyway, leaving two sets of authoritative books.
proposed_resolution: Owner decision: (1) native and authoritative: DAF fund subledger and the DAF-program GL accounts, posting engine, reconciliation, close, fund statements, Schedule D source data; (2) integration: balanced summarized journal export to the sponsor ERP with control-account tie-out (strengthen UNB-ACC-028); (3) defer or exclude: AP, purchasing, AR (except partner fee billing), budgeting, payroll, fixed assets, cross-entity consolidation and translation. Keep transaction-currency FX only for cross-border grant payments.
decision_owner: Program owner (owner-directed scope) with sponsor CFO

title: Requirements attribute ledger, append-only, temporal and replay guarantees to Strata, a schema management tool
description: Strata (kemiller2002/strata) is a pilot-stage declarative PostgreSQL schema management tool: it compiles .sql, diffs against a database, and deploys. It is not an event store, ledger or temporal database. Even so, UNB-ACC-026 requires 'Strata integration' to 'preserve immutable posting, correction links, temporal queries, tenant isolation, replay-safe projections and integrity checks'. UNB-CUST-013 asks for 'Strata-backed append-only persistence', UNB-NAV-044 for 'Strata-integrated evidence', and NAV-T17 for a 'Strata-backed projection rebuild'. The hedges ('gaps ... are blockers') turn every one of these into a permanent blocker. Strata can legitimately help one guarantee: gating destructive schema changes (UNB-IMM-001).
impact: As written, the accounting and NAV requirement set cannot pass its own gates (ACC-ADR-008, NAV-ADR-008, INV-ADR-008 can never close), or teams build a companion component without requirements of its own.
proposed_resolution: Supersede the Strata wording: the ledger component provides append-only posting, correction links, bitemporal queries and integrity checkpoints on PostgreSQL (privilege revocation for UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE, constraint triggers, hash-chained checkpoints), verified by Dokimos tests. Strata is used for declarative schema management and destructive-migration refusal for those tables. No Echelon capability is claimed verified.

title: Illustrative fund-to-fund transfer is not balanced per fund
description: The successor-transfer example posts Dr 1030 (fund = successor) $5,000 / Cr 1030 (fund = origin) $5,000. The entity-level journal balances, but each fund's trial balance is out by $5,000: the successor gains cash with no net-asset credit, and the origin loses cash with no net-asset debit. This contradicts the document's own warning (line 71) and ACC-02 (fund allocations reconcile to sponsor control accounts). ACC-MDL-003 and UNB-ACC-002 require balance 'by book, currency and accounting basis' but never say whether the fund is a self-balancing segment, so the defect cannot be detected by the stated balance property (line 90).
impact: Per-fund statements, capacity and successor splits can drift without any balance check failing. The entity books still balance, so misallocation between donors' funds goes unnoticed.
proposed_resolution: Declare fund (and restriction) as balancing segments; each journal must balance per entity x currency x fund. Transfers post Dr origin net assets (or 3900 transfer-out) / Cr origin cash and Dr successor cash / Cr successor net assets (or 3900 transfer-in), with 3900 netting to zero sponsor-wide. Add a fixture.

title: Two incompatible journal envelopes; one puts a single FundId on the batch header
description: CANONICAL section 3 defines the envelope with line-level FundId, BookId, TenantId and IntegrityCheckpoint. The REQ-X-084 journal-contract schema puts FundId on the batch header, adds KnownAt, EvidenceHash and ClosePeriodId, and has no BookId or TenantId. A header-level FundId cannot represent the multi-fund journals the requirements themselves need (interfund fee, successor split).
impact: Implementers choosing either schema will be incompatible with the other's examples. A header-level fund either blocks transfers or invites splitting one economic event into unlinked journals.
proposed_resolution: Adopt one canonical envelope: fund only at line level; include BookId, TenantId, EffectiveAt, RecordedAt (known-at), ClosePeriodId, EvidenceHash, PolicyVersion, IdempotencyKey and CorrectionOf; retire the other.

title: Fee posting examples contradict each other on who receives the fee
description: CANONICAL models a sponsor fee within one legal entity as an interfund charge (Fund A expense against sponsor operating revenue, eliminated on consolidation). The REQ-X-084 example D and fixtures JRN-06/JRN-07 post Fee Expense / Fee Payable, then Fee Payable / Cash, so cash leaves the entity. That is right for a third-party administrator (for example, the FMR arrangement in batch-1c) but wrong for a sponsor's own fee. No requirement models the fee recipient type.
impact: Sponsor fee revenue could be misstated or double counted, and cash movements implied that never happened externally.
proposed_resolution: Add a fee-recipient discriminator (sponsor internal, third-party administrator, investment manager, advisor, payment rail) with a posting rule per type; add fixtures for each.

title: Fee base undefined: fee-on-fee, double charging and fee timing are not testable
description: UNB-NAV-033 says fees must 'not be charged twice at pool and DAF levels' but no requirement defines the assessment base. Unspecified: the measurement basis (average daily, month-end or other; batch-1b warns against year-end denominators); whether accrued unpaid fees, reservations, provisional contributions (TVF-119) and unsettled proceeds are in the base; whether a DAF-level fee is computed on a NAV that already embeds a pool-level sponsor fee (batch-1d: the Vanguard admin fee is embedded in pool NAV); whether tiers are marginal (DAFgiving360 published tiers) or whole-balance; how minimums apply (Fidelity $100 minimum; the fee-scenario file shows a 100 bps effective rate at $10,000). Fee timing against capacity (FI-25, TVF-011) and fee-versus-grant priority (FI-26, OD-10) are still open.
impact: Fees computed on bases that include accrued fees or embedded pool fees overcharge funds, and the error compounds each period. Small funds can be driven negative by minimums.
proposed_resolution: Add UNB-RCN-FIN-005 (fee base contract). Every fee accrual records basis type, base amount, exclusions applied, NAV version, tier method and minimum; deterministic recomputation must match within zero tolerance.

title: Grant lifecycle still has no funding or liquidation states between reservation and payment
description: TX-11 goes from SponsorApprovedAndReserved directly to TX-12 PaymentInstructionAuthorized, gated only on payee verification and holds. No transition requires settled, unencumbered cash in the paying account. UNB-GFUND-011 and -014 require a funding plan and shortfall handling but name no states; FundingShortfall exists only in research (FI-13). TVF-001 (no reservation or funding states) is recorded as open and the canonical matrix has not resolved it. TVF-073 (a pool liquidity buffer paying grants before unit redemption) is also open.
impact: A payment can be authorized against unsettled or illiquid value, so other funds' or the sponsor's cash covers it: a cross-subsidy and a possible overdraft.
proposed_resolution: Add UNB-RCN-FIN-008: states FundingPlanned, LiquidationPending, Funded, FundingShortfall; PaymentInstructionAuthorized requires Funded (settled cash allocated to the grant), unless a sponsor-approved liquidity-advance policy records the advance as an interfund receivable.

title: Capacity is defined as a projection but reservations need a transactional check
description: ACC-MDL-004 and REQ-X-084 define available-to-recommend capacity as a 'controlled projection', and UNB-NAV-044 rebuilds projections from append-only evidence. REQ-X-022 and FI-05 require capacity to be checked and the reservation created in one serialized operation across all constrained ancestors (financial-core invariant 6). If capacity is read from an eventually consistent projection, two reservations can both pass. The requirements never say that the reservation check must read authoritative state.
impact: Concurrent grants can overcommit a fund or a shared pool or custody account, the defect class UNB-GFUND-021 is meant to prevent.
proposed_resolution: Add UNB-RCN-FIN-009: the reservation command computes capacity inside the same serializable transaction from authoritative ledger and reservation rows, with deterministic lock order across ancestors. Displayed capacity is a separate, labelled projection that is never used for authorization.

title: No allocation method for non-unitized omnibus accounts
description: UNB-INV-002 permits one custody account to support many DAFs through 'explicitly governed omnibus allocation', and REQ-X-023 makes unitization optional. No requirement says how income, realized and unrealized gains, fees, corporate actions and in-kind lots are attributed to each DAF when the omnibus account is not unitized. ACC-10 only says 'independently validated ownership units/rules'. The two choices (lot-level per-fund sub-accounting, or unitization of the omnibus account) have different data models.
impact: Income and gains can be misattributed between donors' funds. Daily cash-flow timing makes pro-rata-by-period-end allocation wrong.
proposed_resolution: Add UNB-RCN-FIN-007: an omnibus account must declare its attribution method (per-fund lot sub-accounting, or unitized). Lot sub-accounting requires every position and lot to carry a fund owner and sum to the custodian position; unitized follows the NAV rules. Mixed or undeclared methods are rejected.

title: Capacity and ledger invariants assume unitization, which REQ-X-023 makes optional
description: FI defines fund value V(f,t) as sum of units x latest struck NAV plus cash, less accrued fees; FI-02 and CTL-018 check sum(units x NAV) = pool NAV. REQ-X-023 and DAF-FUND section 3 say unitization is optional and that segregated portfolios and cash-only funds must be supported. No equivalent valuation or capacity formula exists for segregated or lot-level holdings (price source, staleness haircut, unsettled lots).
impact: Segregated-holding funds have no defined capacity, so implementers will improvise.
proposed_resolution: Generalize V(f,t) to the sum of position valuations under the valuation policy for each holding type; units x NAV is one case.

title: Break blocking rules disagree and thresholds have no owner
description: ACC-MDL-009: 'unbalanced or unexplained breaks block unsupported close certifications' (any amount). UNB-NAV-007: only 'material unexplained breaks prevent final publication'. UNB-NAV-012: 'approved tolerance/rounding policy'. REQ-X-040: materiality escalation with auto-validation of routine items. FI-29: a threshold to be decided. None defines the unit (absolute or bps), the scope (fund, pool, sponsor), the owner, or the handling of immaterial but unexplained breaks. TVF-158 (any break blocks all reservations on a shared account) is still open.
impact: Either close never completes (any $0.01 break blocks) or material breaks pass under loose tolerances. ADV-467 shows tolerances can be silently raised.
proposed_resolution: Single break policy: tolerance (rounding, auto-clear with evidence), materiality (blocks close or publication for the affected scope), and an aged-unexplained escalation path regardless of amount. Thresholds are versioned sponsor parameters owned by the Controller; loosening needs a second approver (CTL-010).

title: Independent attestation of every reconciliation conflicts with auto-pass of routine reconciliations
description: REQ-X-010: an 'independent finance reviewer must attest reconciliations outside the payment chain'. REQ-X-040 and the month-end detail (line 34): 'Routine deterministic reconciliations can auto-pass under versioned finance policy'. Both cannot hold for every reconciliation.
impact: Either human attestation becomes the bottleneck of month-end close or the REQ-X-010 control is quietly bypassed.
proposed_resolution: See RCC-FIN-004: independent human attestation applies to the policy (rules, tolerances, matching logic) and to exceptions and close certification; deterministic passes are evidence, not attestations.

title: Returned-contribution treatment contradicts itself and presumes a donor receivable
description: REQ-X-009: 'returned funds trigger receivable'. FI-23 and the FI concurrency table: 'Donor receivable'. The REQ-X-084 example A: 'Dr a sponsor-approved return/reversal account'. TX-05: 'compensating debit and holds'. Whether a returned ACH payment ever produced a completed gift, and whether the sponsor has an enforceable claim against a donor for a voluntary gift, are legal questions (counsel). Recognizing a receivable that is probably uncollectible is an accounting question (CPA). TVF-006 and TVF-159 are still open.
impact: Fund statements may show donor receivables that do not exist legally. Loss allocation between the fund, other unitholders and the sponsor is undefined.
proposed_resolution: Replace 'receivable' with a neutral 'returned-contribution exposure' fact; the posting is chosen by a CPA-approved policy (reversal of contribution, receivable with allowance, or sponsor loss) and the loss-bearer by OD-20. Counsel confirms the completed-gift and claim questions.

title: 'Refund' paths could distribute accepted DAF assets to donors
description: ADV-133 expects a 'governed successor/refund disposition' for returns to a closed fund. The chart includes '2050 Refund/return liability' without a definition. REQ-X-070 item 4 includes 'refund and wage-deduction exceptions'. No requirement separates (a) returning property that was never accepted or never a completed gift from (b) paying accepted DAF assets to a donor or other natural person. Case (b) is a taxable distribution under IRC 4966(c)(1)(A) (statute; OB-01), with sponsor and manager excise exposure.
impact: A refund workflow outside the grant controls could make taxable distributions to natural persons.
proposed_resolution: Add UNB-RCN-FIN-013: after acceptance, value leaves a fund only through the grant lifecycle to an eligible grantee or a governed transfer. 'Refund' is restricted to pre-acceptance returns of non-completed gifts and payroll over-withholding before acceptance, under counsel-approved policy. Rename 2050 accordingly.

title: Closing (100%) grants, proceeds-linked grants and the percentage fixing point remain unresolved
description: UNB-GFUND-002 enumerates percentage bases but not the residual-sweep '100% of fund' grant (FI-15) or the proceeds-of-gift grant (FI-39). UNB-GFUND-013 leaves the lock point to policy, and GF-ADR-002 / OD-07 are still open. FI-10 proposes fixing once at approval. Prior findings TVF-108, TVF-118, TVF-182 and TVF-191 are open and not resolved by the requirements.
impact: Closing grants fixed at approval are wrong by construction. The grant state machine cannot represent amount-unknown approvals.
proposed_resolution: Adopt FI-10 single fixing with an explicit FixingEvent per amount mode; add ResidualSweep and ProceedsLinked amount modes with fixing at last settlement; sponsor owner decides the default (OD-07).

title: Per-grant liquidation framing persists for unitized pools
description: UNB-GFUND-011 requires a per-grant funding plan with 'pool redemption cutoffs ... and tax-lot rules', which implies per-grant trades. FI-14 (rev 2) says units are redeemed internally at forward NAV and the pool trades net across all flows; per-grant trades exist only for separately managed sources. TVC-043 and TVF-157 recorded this; the requirement text was not updated.
impact: Per-grant trading in pools raises trading cost and creates unit/cash mismatches.
proposed_resolution: Restate UNB-GFUND-011 by source type: pool sources produce unit-redemption instructions at the next strike; segregated sources produce trade instructions with lot selection.

title: Canonical text of REQ-X-059, -067 and -070 is boilerplate with no testable obligations
description: The canonical entries for REQ-X-065..070 share one sentence ('Extend the one Unbound component monolith with ... audit'). The detail files list topics and synthetic case names ('Fee double charge, rebate, ...'; 'Cases: pending asset transfer, restricted shares, ...') without expected outcomes, thresholds or states.
impact: These requirements cannot be accepted or rejected by a test; traceability from REQ-X to tests is nominal.
proposed_resolution: Rewrite each as normative statements with Given/When/Then acceptance criteria (the gap requirements and refinements here cover the financial parts).

title: ADV-435..ADV-470 all have the same boilerplate expected outcome
description: All 36 month-end adversarial cases end with 'expected: authoritative controls, explicit exception, correct scope, immutable evidence and governed recovery'. None names the resulting close state, blocked scope, posting, or notification.
impact: The cases cannot be turned into Dokimos assertions without re-specification.
proposed_resolution: Give each case an expected close-state, affected scope, financial effect and audit record (see DKS-FIN scenarios for examples).

title: Journal fixtures balance but cannot test fund, entity or currency balancing
description: Recomputed every fixture: JRN-01..JRN-10 each have debits = credits (100/100, 80/80, 80/80, 100/100, 100 = 90+10/100, 5/5, 5/5, 80/80, 100/100, 100/100); no imbalance. However, the CSV has no entity, fund, restriction or currency columns, so the per-fund and per-currency rules (ACC-MDL-003, ACC-01) are untestable. The NetImbalanceUSD column is a literal, not derived. There are no fixtures for fund-to-fund transfer, interfund fee and elimination, unit subscription and redemption, FX, returned ACH, noncash gift with fees, or correction-of-correction.
impact: Fixtures give false assurance; the RCF-FIN-010 defect would pass.
proposed_resolution: Extend fixtures with line-level dimensions and the missing cases (UNB-RCN-FIN-014); compute imbalance by script per entity x currency x fund.

title: NAV worked example mislabels net assets as assets
description: The example says that after the $5,200 subscription 'the resulting assets are $1,045,200'. Assets become $1,055,200 (1,050,000 + 5,200) and net assets $1,045,200 (liabilities $10,000). The unit arithmetic is correct: 1,045,200 / 100,500 = 10.40; 5,200 / 10.40 = 500; 125 x 10.40 = 1,300; 1,039,000 / 100,000 = 10.39.
impact: A test written against the wrong label would assert the wrong balance-sheet line.
proposed_resolution: Change 'assets' to 'net assets' in the example.

title: DAF fund accounting detail file cites the wrong companion requirements
description: The detail file says 'Companion REQ-X-017..022', but the canonical register attaches it as REQ-X-023.
impact: Back-traceability from the detail to the canonical requirement is broken.
proposed_resolution: Correct the header to REQ-X-023.

title: Duplicate: REQ-X-041 is defined twice with different text
description: Two headings for REQ-X-041 have different normative text: the first says 'in-process' and 'evidence-based resolution verification'; the second says 'risk-based SLAs and metrics'.
impact: Ambiguous baseline for the exception component that the FIN reconciliation workflow relies on.
proposed_resolution: Merge into one definition; keep the superset with explicit provenance.

title: Duplicate: the append-only correction rule appears at least eight times with different required attributes
description: UNB-ACC-003 requires approval; ACC-MDL-002 requires bitemporal dates; UNB-IMM-002 requires reason, actor and evidence; UNB-NAV-042 requires reconciliation to the original. No single correction contract exists.
impact: Implementations satisfy different subsets; tests diverge.
proposed_resolution: Define one correction contract (target, kind, reason, actor, approval, effective and recorded times, evidence) referenced by all families.

title: Duplicate: cash/liquidity distinctions are restated with inconsistent vocabulary
description: The same distinction (settled cash, unsettled proceeds, encumbered, committed, available) is repeated with different terms: available-to-recommend, available-to-grant, grantable capacity, spendable cash, eligible available-to-recommend balance.
impact: Donor-facing labels and API fields diverge; UNB-GFUND-002 offers 'available-to-recommend' as a percentage base without a single definition.
proposed_resolution: One glossary term and formula (generalized C(f,t)), referenced everywhere.

title: Payroll and employer-matching contributions raise unaddressed substantiation and benefit questions
description: REQ-X-070 covers payroll batches, employer matching and 'correct charitable receipt' but does not address: how 170(f)(8)/(18) acknowledgment is satisfied for payroll-deducted DAF gifts (pay-stub substantiation rules exist in regulation; counsel to confirm that they satisfy the DAF-specific statement); whether employer matching into an employee's DAF is permitted under employer programs and how corporate and employee attribution is acknowledged; and refunds of wage deductions (see RCF-FIN-021).
impact: Defective substantiation across many small recurring gifts; possible benefit issues.
proposed_resolution: Counsel decision record before REQ-X-070 is made normative; keep partner-first boundary.

title: Performance requirements have no baseline volumes
description: UNB-IMM-010 requires '10x grant surge ... at defined scales' and UNB-ACC-036 'high-volume posting' but no baseline transactions/day, fund count or history length is given.
impact: The requirements cannot be verified.
proposed_resolution: State baseline volumes per sponsor tier as configuration owned by architecture.

title: Monthly statements by default for every fund is a convention, not an outcome
description: REQ-X-032 makes monthly generation the default for every eligible fund. The outcome (donors see accurate, reconciled as-of positions; sponsors meet any disclosure they have committed to) can be met by an always-available portal view from close snapshots plus sponsor-chosen periodic statements (often quarterly). A forced monthly cadence multiplies the statement, approval and delivery work in REQ-X-040.
impact: Unneeded volume of artifacts, approvals and delivery cases.
proposed_resolution: Default cadence is a sponsor parameter; generate on schedule or on demand from immutable close snapshots.

title: Seven-year retention floor is presented as a fixed rule
description: The requirements state a 'seven-year financial retention floor'. The regulatory baseline (OB-28: IRC 6001, statute; Rev. Proc. 97-22, IRS guidance) has no fixed seven-year federal rule; records are kept as long as material. Seven years is a reasonable sponsor policy but should be a parameter with its legal basis.
impact: Records needed longer (for example, basis records for unsold assets, open disposal periods, litigation) could be disposed of at seven years.
proposed_resolution: Make retention a policy parameter per record class, with a seven-year default and event-based extensions.

title: Donor annual summaries must not imply nonitemizer deduction eligibility for DAF gifts
description: From tax year 2026 the nonitemizer cash deduction (IRC 170(p), statute; IR-2026-135 IRS guidance) excludes DAF contributions, and itemizers face a 0.5% floor (OB-22). The FIN requirements and the daf-landscape annual summaries (CON-REC-15) contain no rule preventing donor-facing summaries or AI assistance from implying eligibility.
impact: Misleading donor tax communications.
proposed_resolution: Annual summaries carry counsel-approved, effective-dated disclosures; AI assistance may not state deductibility conclusions.

title: One-system invariant contradicts per-partner dedicated infrastructure
description: UNB-PLAT-008/UNB-TEN-002 require dedicated-infrastructure partner deployments (Profile C) selected per partner, while REQ-X-020 requires 'one deployable application and one authoritative transactional financial/security core', the one-system decision requires 'a single coordinated deployment' and acceptance item 7 says any proposal for 'a second deployable, ledger ... must be rejected'. A dedicated-infrastructure partner is by definition a second running deployment with its own authoritative database. Neither document defines whether 'one system' means one codebase/release train or one runtime instance.
impact: As written the requirement set cannot be satisfied: either Profile C is forbidden by REQ-X-057 or REQ-X-057 is violated by every Profile C partner. Engineers will pick an interpretation silently.
proposed_resolution: Define 'one system' as: one codebase, one domain model, one release version applied to all deployments, one command/policy/ledger implementation. Define a 'deployment cell' (one runtime instance plus its authoritative stores) and permit N cells running the identical release. State explicitly that Profile C is a dedicated cell, not a fork, and that cross-cell operations are explicit inter-cell messages (see RCF-PLT-002/003). Alternatively remove Profile C until a signed contract requires it.

title: Global charity hold has no serialization point across partner databases
description: REQ-X-020 requires 'a provable serialization point' between global charity/hold publication and payment release, with holds binding on releases ordered after their durable commit. Charity facts and holds are shared across partners (UNB-KNOW-012), but grant reservations and payment release live in each partner's authoritative store, which under Profiles B and C is a different database or infrastructure. No requirement says where the global hold is committed, how it reaches each partner store, or how a release in partner database X proves it observed hold version N.
impact: A release in one partner database can commit after a sanctions/eligibility hold was published globally but before it was propagated, producing a payment to a held recipient (potential unlawful distribution).
proposed_resolution: Add a requirement: every global hold has a monotonically increasing hold-publication version; each cell's release gate must read the hold registry synchronously (fail closed on unavailability) or verify that its locally replicated hold watermark is >= the latest published version obtained in the same gate; record the observed watermark on the release record. Add Dokimos scenario DKS-PLT-002.

title: Sponsor-level books and cross-partner transfers span databases despite single-transaction rule
description: REQ-X-021 coordinates multi-component financial operations 'within one authoritative transaction' and REQ-X-057 requires one ledger 'partitioned and reconciled by legal sponsor'. UNB-TEN-020 lets one sponsor serve several partners, and the persistence design requires cross-partner fund transfers as 'two independently authorized records ... not an implicit cross-database join or distributed transaction'. ADR-010 (sponsor-level books when a sponsor serves multiple segregated partners) is open. Pooled investment/NAV across partners of the same sponsor is therefore split across stores with no atomicity or reconciliation rule.
impact: Sponsor consolidated balances, pooled NAV and successor/transfer movements can be half-applied (debit without credit) across partner stores.
proposed_resolution: Decide the partition key of the authoritative ledger: legal sponsor (recommended) not distribution partner. If partners must be physically separated, require a two-phase transfer state machine (TransferOutPending -> TransferInRecorded -> Reconciled) with idempotent inter-cell messages, a suspense account per sponsor and a daily zero-sum reconciliation control.

title: Row-level tenancy assumed by ordering design but not approved as isolation profile
description: PARTNER-SEGREGATION says a shared-schema/row-level-security model 'is not approved as a default isolation profile'. The component-monolith ordering design states 'Shared process/database requires tenant-scoped authorization and queries' and ADV-079 tests 'Shared database query accidentally omits tenant predicate', which only exists in a row-level model.
impact: Implementers following REQ-X-020 acceptance will build row-predicate tenancy that the tenancy requirements forbid, or test a model that will not ship.
proposed_resolution: State in REQ-X-020 that tenant scoping is by schema/database binding through the connection broker (UNB-TEN-004/005) and replace ADV-079 with 'connection bound to wrong schema/database' and 'pooled session retains previous search_path'.

title: The tenant unit is undefined: partner versus sponsor
description: UNB-TEN-001 makes the tenant the 'partner'; UNB-TEN-020 says sponsor and partner are separate dimensions and a sponsor may serve several partners; but REQ-X-024, REQ-X-048, REQ-X-053 and REQ-X-057 speak of 'sponsor/tenant isolation', 'sponsor-scoped' and 'cross-sponsor' leakage as if the sponsor were the tenant. The isolation boundary, the ledger partition and the policy scope are therefore different keys in different documents.
impact: Data that must be shared within a sponsor (policy, pooled investments, charity reviews) may be isolated, and data that must be isolated between partners of one sponsor may be shared.
proposed_resolution: Add a glossary requirement (gap UNB-RCN-PLT-001) defining Tenant, LegalSponsor, DistributionPartner, Program and Cell, the isolation key for each data class, and which classes may cross partners within one sponsor.

title: Three isolation profiles plus live A->B->C migration mandated before any partner evidence
description: The decision text says 'No partner is assumed to require a specific tier without evidence', yet UNB-PLAT-008 and UNB-TEN-002 make all three profiles mandatory simultaneously, and UNB-TEN-012/013 require zero-loss migration between all of them, including 'Partner migration with in-flight payments'. Every engineering test (cross-tenant SQL, pooled connection leakage, selective restore, noisy neighbour) is tripled. UNB-TEN-018 itself admits the database engine and schema-count behaviour are unbenchmarked.
impact: Large fixed cost and test surface before the first customer; Profile A carries known shared-backup restore and noisy-neighbour caveats that the requirements then have to compensate for.
proposed_resolution: Make one profile the default (recommended: database-per-partner on managed infrastructure, Profile B). Keep A and C as gated options activated only by a signed contractual requirement and the UNB-TEN-018 benchmark; migration requirements apply only between activated profiles.

title: Append-only, bitemporal and replay responsibilities attributed to Strata, a schema-management tool
description: UNB-PLAT-007 and UNB-TEC-STRATA-001..004 bind Strata into authoritative event persistence, append-only corrections, bitemporal history, deterministic replay and tenant migration, and the architecture gate says a discovered limitation 'is a design blocker to escalate, not permission to substitute'. The Strata repository is a pilot declarative PostgreSQL schema compile/diff/deploy tool; it does not provide an event store, ledger or temporal query capability.
impact: The gate makes the persistence design permanently blocked, or forces Strata to be stretched into an event store it is not.
proposed_resolution: Re-scope Strata to schema lifecycle (compile, diff, governed deploy of per-tenant schemas and append-only privileges). Move append-only enforcement, bitemporal history and replay to an ADR-selected persistence component with its own verification. Amend the gate so a verified mismatch triggers an owner decision rather than a permanent block.

title: Technology mandates still SHALL despite ADR-gating decision and noncommercial licences
description: REQ-X-012 says stack/event-sourcing selection 'stays ADR-gated' and OD-16 recommended moving Limen/Forma/Folio/WASM to an ADR-gated candidate list, but UNB-PLAT-002/003/006/007 remain unconditional SHALL mandates. TVC-002 notes the components are PolyForm Noncommercial licensed; REQ-X-050 still asks to 'confirm commercial license suitability'. TVC-002/OD-16 remain open and the platform standard was not updated.
impact: A commercial product could be built on components it is not licensed to use commercially; requirements text pre-empts the ADR process.
proposed_resolution: Resolve OD-16. Rewrite UNB-PLAT-002/003/006/007 as 'preferred candidate, subject to ADR, capability verification and an executed commercial licence', with a named fallback per component.

title: Folio mandated for documents while Typst is the preferred PDF renderer
description: UNB-PLAT-003 says all enterprise documents and statements SHALL use Folio. REQ-X-033/034 make Typst 'via validated Folio-compatible adapter' the preferred PDF candidate. Folio is an HTML/print-CSS component system; Folio's own Unbound review states Folio HTML and Typst 'do not have demonstrated direct interoperability'. Two renderers with different layout models would be required for the same statements.
impact: Duplicate template investment, statements that render differently by channel, and an undefined meaning of 'Folio-compatible adapter'.
proposed_resolution: Choose one issuance renderer for as-issued financial documents via ADR (Folio P2 Chromium or Typst), and limit the other to non-issued previews. Update UNB-PLAT-003 accordingly.

title: Forma treated as a widget runtime and brand owner
description: UI requirements specify 'Forma widgets' with versioned manifests, capability discovery, host-origin validation, embed tokens and telemetry, and require 'Balanced Charcoal and Bronze' tokens as Forma design standards. The Forma repository describes itself as zero-component-runtime and brand-neutral (behaviour belongs to the consuming application; brand comes from a manifest; Forma ships none). REQ-X-055 correctly says 'Forma only presentation', so the documents disagree.
impact: Widget security, embedding and data contracts could be left unowned on the assumption Forma supplies them.
proposed_resolution: Assign widget manifest, embed token, origin validation and data contract ownership to an Unbound/Limen component; reference Forma only for markup, CSS, tokens and accessibility contracts; express Charcoal/Bronze as an Unbound brand manifest.

title: Visual WYSIWYG email designer is not needed for transactional DAF notices
description: REQ-X-029/031/052 require a WYSIWYG/block email designer, Forma Studio authoring, a typed expression language with conditionals and repetition, optional raw sanitized HTML mode and email-client compatibility validation. The Forma email designer is itself only a proposed requirement whose 'first consumer' is Unbound, so Unbound is commissioning a new reusable product. DAF email is predominantly transactional (grant status, statement available, security notices) where content and mandatory clauses are fixed and branding comes from the Brand Kit (REQ-X-030). No evidence in daf-landscape shows sponsors selecting providers on email authoring.
