impact: Large build and security surface (HTML injection, image hosting, client compatibility, accessibility of authored content) for low business value; delays core grant and statement workflows.
proposed_resolution: Supersede REQ-X-029/031/052 for the initial scope with a constrained template model: fixed per-event block layouts, Brand Kit theming, editable text slots with typed tokens, locale variants, preview and approval (see refinement RR-REQ-X-029-r1). Re-open a visual designer only on documented sponsor demand.

title: Duplicate: six overlapping email template requirements
description: Template override, revision history, visual styling, brand kit, designer ownership and expression language are split over six requirements that each restate token typing, mandatory clauses, previews, approval and as-sent history.
impact: Inconsistent acceptance criteria and ownership as each is refined separately.
proposed_resolution: Merge into two: (1) Communication template lifecycle and as-sent history (027+028+052 token subset), (2) Brand Kit (030). Retire 029/031 per RCF-PLT-011.

title: Seven-year retention floor has no stated legal basis and conflicts with the no-invented-periods rule
description: REQ-X-036 is an 'owner-directed policy' applied as a 'nonwaivable platform floor' to all financially material records in every channel (REQ-X-037). No statute, regulation or IRS guidance is cited; SOC2-023 says 'do not invent universal retention periods'. Earlier research (TVC-016) recorded a candidate 10-year OFAC-driven period and an 'as long as returns can be examined' basis, both unconfirmed. The floor is explicitly not a legal conclusion, but it is applied to notes, IVR and communications where privacy minimisation may require shorter periods.
impact: Possible over-retention of personal data (privacy exposure) and possible under-retention where a longer obligation applies but is not modelled because the floor looks authoritative.
proposed_resolution: Keep seven years as a sponsor-contract business policy parameter (owner: GC) rather than a platform legal floor; require each record class to cite authority type (statute/regulation/IRS guidance/contract/sponsor policy) and counsel-approved period; needs counsel on IRC 6001 record-keeping for exempt organizations, OFAC recordkeeping period, state charitable-solicitation rules and privacy deletion precedence.

title: Every expired record becomes a human disposition review
description: Expiration 'triggers governed disposition review, never automatic deletion' and a Retention Console 'review queue' is specified. At platform scale this is a per-record human queue that grows with every statement and email.
impact: Unbounded backlog; in practice records are never disposed, defeating privacy minimisation.
proposed_resolution: Approve disposition per record class and period as a batch policy decision (dual approval), then execute deterministically with a pre-disposition hold/dependency recheck and sampled verification; only exceptions route to humans.

title: Duplicate: the retention floor and hold semantics restated in three requirements
description: REQ-X-036, 037 and 038 each restate the seven-year floor, longest-obligation precedence, legal-hold propagation and 'no automatic deletion'.
impact: Three places to update when counsel changes the rule.
proposed_resolution: Keep REQ-X-037 (classification matrix) and REQ-X-038 (engine); fold REQ-X-036 into 037 as one class-level policy row.

title: Adversarial scenario IDs ADV-843..ADV-890 defined in several files with different content
description: Beyond the known triple definition of REQ-X-054/055, 48 ADV identifiers are defined more than once with different scenarios, e.g. ADV-843 is 'assistant suggests nonexistent setting', 'assistant describes hidden setting to unauthorized user' and 'proactive check duplicates existing exception' in three files; ADV-867 likewise.
impact: Test results cannot be traced to a unique scenario; a pass on one ADV-843 may be reported for another.
proposed_resolution: Renumber per file with a file-scoped prefix or a registry allocator; reject duplicate IDs in CI (REQ-X-082 static gate).

title: About 700 adversarial scenarios share one boilerplate expected result per file
description: In 20 detail files in this domain every ADV line has the identical expected outcome (e.g. all 30 in the AI contracts file end 'expected: fail-closed guidance, scoped discovery, versioned source, authorized execution'; all 60 in the platform-wide AI file share one). The stimulus varies but the oracle does not, so none of these are executable tests.
impact: The acceptance basis of REQ-X-037..055 is illusory; Dokimos or any harness cannot derive pass/fail.
proposed_resolution: Require per-scenario expected state, rejected command/error code, audit record and invariant (as in Output 6) before an ADV ID counts as acceptance; mark existing ones 'stimulus only'.

title: AI assistance contract has a field list but no standard schema
description: REQ-X-051 requires machine-readable assistance metadata for every API, input, configuration, widget and email block. The detail file lists ~33 field names for AssistantCapabilityContract and ~20 for FieldHelp but gives no types, required/optional status, enumerations, identifier format, versioning rule, publication location or relation to the API contract of UNB-API-STD-001. 'Assistant-ready' has no measurable definition.
impact: Each component will invent its own shape; drift checks (ADV-744) and caller-scoped discovery cannot be implemented.
proposed_resolution: Define one JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) published with the API contract, with a minimal required core (id, version, owner, kind, purpose, inputs schema ref, side effects enum, authority class, confirmation requirement, reversibility enum, unknown-state semantics) and optional editorial annotations; generate from F# types; see refinement RR-REQ-X-051-r1.

title: Four incompatible AI autonomy taxonomies
description: Authority tiers A0-A5 (SPONSOR-AUTHORITY), assistance levels L0-L3 (REQ-X-051), proactive risk Tier 0-4 (REQ-X-055) and decision-routing Tier 1-3 (REQ-X-017) overlap: 'Tier 1' means deterministic policy decision in REQ-X-017 but 'safe deterministic enrichment' in REQ-X-055; L3 'Execute' has no mapping to A2/A3; the decision matrix assigns 'Prepare payment instruction' to A3 without saying whether an agent may perform A3.
impact: The human approval boundary for agents differs by document; an agent could be authorised under one taxonomy for an action another forbids.
proposed_resolution: Adopt one authority matrix (action class x actor type {deterministic policy, AI agent, human} -> allowed/proposal-only/prohibited) with A0-A5 as the single scale, and map L- and Tier- terms to it or retire them.

title: AIN-003 requires humans for all grant decisions; REQ-X-017 permits zero-human routine approval
description: AIN-003: 'Reserved legal, grant, financial, trading and payment decisions require authorized humans'. REQ-X-017 acceptance: 'A complete low-risk grant passes deterministic rules and incurs zero AI calls and zero human touches'. This is the TVC-003/OD-01 question re-appearing in a newer requirement that was not reconciled.
impact: Either automated routine approval is unlawful under AIN-003, or AIN-003 is silently ignored.
proposed_resolution: Reword AIN-003 to 'reserved decisions not covered by a board-delegated deterministic policy (OD-01) require authorized humans; AI never approves'. Keep OD-01 open with GC.

title: Duplicate: AI assistance specified about nine times
description: UNB-AI-STD-001..003, AIN-001..036, REQ-X-051, REQ-X-053, three REQ-X-054 and three REQ-X-055 entries repeat the same principles (no self-approval, provenance, fact vs inference, caller scope, prompt-injection isolation) with drifting wording.
impact: Conflicting acceptance and taxonomy drift (RCF-PLT-019).
proposed_resolution: Consolidate into: AI authority boundary (one), assistance contract (REQ-X-051), assistance UX (one), proactive detection (one). Retire the rest as superseded.

title: AI help on every input field is unbounded scope
description: REQ-X-054 requires contextual AI help 'on every documented input, API, action, configuration' and 'every eligible field'. Most fields (name, address, amount) need deterministic validation messages, not model calls.
impact: Cost, latency and evaluation burden for no outcome gain; harder to keep help in sync.
proposed_resolution: Require deterministic contract-generated help for all fields; reserve AI explanation for configuration, policy, exception and case surfaces selected by user-research evidence.

title: Staff UI is organised by department and queue rather than by goal and exception
description: Despite PRINCIPLES step 4 and AIN-001 ('not an inherited department workflow'), the staff experience defines 13 role workspaces mirroring departments (Grants Specialist 'grant case queue', Contributions Specialist, Compliance, Finance), REQ-X-049 makes Work Queue Management 'a first-class dashboard area' with My Work/Team Queue/Supervisor Command Center, and the queue-first versus account-first question is left as an open research item. No requirement sets a straight-through-processing objective or requires that a work item exist only when deterministic processing cannot finish.
impact: Rebuilds the legacy back office in a new UI; human touches become the default path.
proposed_resolution: Make the primary staff surface an exception inbox of WorkItems that exist only for (a) deterministic-policy hold, (b) evidence missing, (c) reserved-authority decision; require each WorkItem to name the outcome blocked and the rule that created it; add STP-rate and touches-per-grant metrics (gap UNB-RCN-PLT-006).

title: Duplicate: overlapping command centers, dashboards and widgets
description: Sponsor Command Center (UX-S01), Supervisor Command Center (REQ-X-049), Executive assurance overview, Control Operations Home, AssuranceDashboard, Health Center (REQ-X-055), Risk Heatmap, Performance & Learning and source-health dashboards (UNB-KNOW-039) overlap. Widget lists repeat under different names: ControlHealth/ControlHealthSummary, MyControlTasks/MyExceptions, MissingEvidence/EvidenceCompleteness, AgentAuthorizationFailures/AgentBoundaryViolations, FinancialReconciliationStatus/NAVReconciliation, GrantEligibilityHold/CharityEligibilityHold.
impact: Parallel metric definitions and inconsistent counts across screens; more UI to keep accessible.
proposed_resolution: One widget catalog keyed by semantic metric ID (REQ-X-043); one sponsor home composed from it per role; delete renamed duplicates.

title: Duplicate: five case/work-item models
description: Outcome case (AIN-009), service request/case orchestration (ADM-015/016), WorkItem (REQ-X-048), deficiency case (MON-007/OPS lifecycle), exception case (REQ-X-041) and 'Human Escalation Inbox' each define their own lifecycle, while the one-system decision requires 'One work orchestration and case queue'.
impact: Five state machines for the same human-attention concept; items fall between them.
proposed_resolution: One Case aggregate with typed case kinds (service, exception, control deficiency, agent escalation) sharing one lifecycle and routing; domain-specific states live in the subject aggregate.

title: Dashboards deferred in REQ-X-043 but first-class in REQ-X-049/050
description: REQ-X-043 treats 'role-based dashboard UX, embedded widgets, formal report catalog/designer and scheduling as explicitly deferred'; REQ-X-049 and REQ-X-050 specify them now as first-class.
impact: Release planning conflict.
proposed_resolution: Record a single phase decision; REQ-X-049/050 inherit REQ-X-043's deferral unless the owner reverses it.

title: Screen state set omits Unknown/Uncertain and Failed
description: UNB-UX-003 requires pending, completed, blocked, failed and uncertain states to be distinct. Every screen contract uses 'Loading, Empty, Draft, Ready, PendingApproval, Blocked, Stale, Error, Completed', which has no Uncertain/Unknown or domain Failed state. A provider Unknown payment outcome would have to render as Error or Completed.
impact: Donor or staff sees a payment as failed or completed when the outcome is unknown, leading to duplicate grants or false assurances.
proposed_resolution: Separate UI loading states from domain outcome states; require each screen to render the subject's domain state vocabulary (including Unknown) from the authoritative state machine.

title: Phone completion mandated for every journey including heavy administration
description: UNB-PLAT-004 requires essential completion on a phone for compliance, partner and administrative experiences; this includes control design, routing configuration, reconciliation break review and template authoring.
impact: Large design and test cost for tasks nobody performs on a phone; risk of cramped financial review screens.
proposed_resolution: Classify tasks: donor/advisor/successor and approve/decline decisions phone-complete; configuration, reconciliation and authoring desktop-first with phone read and approve; record the class per task in the persona-by-journey matrix.

title: Document accessibility escapes through 'where supported'
description: UNB-PLAT-005 sets WCAG 2.2 AA plus legal obligations, but UNB-DOC-003 tests Folio outputs 'where supported' and UNB-PLAT-003 applies Folio 'where technically supported'; the dashboard assessment records that tagged PDF/PDF-UA is not assumed present. No requirement guarantees an accessible equivalent of each issued statement.
impact: Donors relying on assistive technology may receive inaccessible tax and statement documents.
proposed_resolution: Require for every issued document either a tagged accessible PDF or an equivalent accessible HTML rendition from the same snapshot, delivered at the same time; needs counsel on ADA/Section 508 applicability to sponsors.

title: 90-control master matrix is 30 copies of three templates marked Designed
description: All 90 rows share three objectives, three evidence strings and three SOC 2 candidates (CC5/CC6, CC7, CC5/CC7); api_scope and agent_scope are '<domain> governed APIs' / '<domain> bounded agents'. Every row is status 'Designed', although the governance note calls them proposed and MATRIX-007/SOC2-008 forbid advancing status without observed evidence. No row maps CC1-CC4, CC8 (change), CC9 (vendor), availability, processing integrity, confidentiality or privacy criteria.
impact: Overstated design maturity in the artifact meant to prevent overstated assurance; coverage gaps hidden.
proposed_resolution: Reset status to Proposed; drop the 90 templated rows in favour of the 46 specific controls plus risk-driven additions; build a TSC criterion-to-control map with explicit not-applicable decisions.

title: The 1,893 keyword-generated requirement-to-control links are mostly not meaningful
description: All 1,893 rows carry the identical rationale 'Keyword and domain candidate', identical evidence text and status; 444 of 494 requirements got exactly four links. Sampled errors: UNB-PLAT-005 (WCAG) -> role provisioning, revocation, MFA, tenant isolation; wave 1 maps it to an eligibility control UNB-CTRL-016; UNB-PLAT-002 (use Forma) -> sponsor decision authority, segregation of duties, grant approval; UNB-TEN-020 (sponsor/partner modelling) -> legal rule publication, exemptions, sanctions; GOV-AUTH-019 (no live payments) is not linked to UNB-SCTRL-030 (live payment prohibition), which together with UNB-SCTRL-029 has zero links. The repo itself says they are 'not validated' (wave 3), yet the CSV is the only artifact claiming SOC2-007 coverage.
impact: Reviewers will treat the CSV as coverage; real gaps (payment controls) are masked by noise.
proposed_resolution: Quarantine the CSV as 'machine candidates, do not cite'. Replace with control-first mapping: each control owner lists the requirements the control enforces (expected tens, not thousands), plus requirement-side 'no control needed' decisions for non-risk requirements such as UI framework choice.

title: 646 of 1,140 requirement IDs have no control link or non-applicability decision
description: Both mapping waves covered only 15 documents (494 IDs). Families with no link include REQ-X (84), ADM (49), UNB-KNOW (40), AIN (36), OPS (32), MON (24), INT (20), UNB-PAY (10), UNB-IMM (10), UNB-API-STD (6), UNB-DOC (5). SOC2-007 requires every requirement to map or record non-applicability.
impact: Payment, immutability, AI authority and API requirements, the highest-risk ones, have no traced control.
proposed_resolution: Prioritise control-first mapping for payment, authority, tenant isolation, AI tool authorization and evidence integrity requirements; record explicit not-applicable for presentation-only requirements.

title: Three control lifecycle vocabularies
description: SOC2-019: Proposed, Designed, Implemented, Operating, Tested, Deficient, Remediating, AuditorReviewed. MATRIX-007: same without Deficient/Remediating as states. Executable assurance: Specified -> Reviewed -> Implemented -> Operating -> IndependentlyTested -> AuditorReviewed; SCTRL and MON rows use 'Specified'. CONTROL-OPERATIONS defines a 16-step lifecycle (PROPOSE..AUDIT).
impact: Status reports cannot be compared; 'Specified' and 'Designed' may be read as equal maturity.
proposed_resolution: One control state machine (design status, operating status and test status as separate orthogonal fields) referenced by all control artifacts.

title: Missing-evidence control relies on a heartbeat from the monitored system
description: UNB-SCTRL-041 evaluates 'ControlHeartbeatEvaluated' emitted per interval, while GAP-V06 states missing-log detection must not be 'a heartbeat produced only by the system being monitored'. The specific control was not updated.
impact: A compromised or crashed producer also stops the heartbeat evaluator path, so silence can look healthy.
proposed_resolution: Require the expected-evidence schedule and evaluator to run on an independently deployed observer with separate credentials, alerting on absence (dead-man switch).

title: A full GRC product is specified inside the DAF platform
description: Control Designer, Test Planner, Risk Heatmap, Regulatory Applicability, Auditor Requests, Monitoring Configuration and 12 more screens, a 16-step control lifecycle and 10 assurance screens go well beyond 'evidence by design'. The outcome needed is that the product emits trustworthy evidence and detects missing evidence; control design, sampling and audit workflow are commodity GRC functions.
impact: Months of build on internal tooling that competes with core DAF workflows; more surface to secure and audit.
proposed_resolution: Keep in product: evidence emission, evidence integrity, expected-evidence monitor, deficiency cases in the shared Case model, Folio evidence export. Use an external GRC or spreadsheet register for control design/testing until scale justifies building; needs owner decision.

title: SOC 1 for fund-accounting controls still absent from the governance directive
description: TVC-027 recorded that fund accounting relied on by sponsors' auditors needs SOC 1 Type II. REQ-X-073 mentions 'SOC 1/2 scope', but the SOC 2 directive, master matrix and executable controls remain SOC 2 only; TVC-027 is therefore only partly addressed.
impact: Sponsors' financial-statement auditors may not be able to rely on the platform's controls.
proposed_resolution: Add an assurance-scope requirement: SOC 1 Type II for ICFR-relevant services and SOC 2 for security/availability/confidentiality, scoped with a CPA.

title: Duplicate: SOC2, MATRIX, OPS, MON and GOV-AUTH families restate the same rules
description: Missing evidence is not a pass (SOC2-027, MATRIX-004, OPS-010, MON-004); no false assurance claims (SOC2-036, MATRIX-011, OPS-022, MON-024); segregation (GOV-AUTH-004, OPS-005, MON-008). OPS, AIN, INT and ADM are also each defined twice (Markdown and CSV) with no declared authoritative copy.
impact: Drift between copies; reviewers cannot tell which text governs.
proposed_resolution: Keep SOC2-* as the directive, MON-* as capability requirements, delete MATRIX/OPS restatements; declare the CSV generated from the Markdown (or vice versa).

title: REQ-X-058..077 normative text is identical boilerplate
description: REQ-X-071, 072 and 073 have word-for-word identical normative statements differing only in the GAP reference; the detail files share a template that, for vendor SOC assurance, requires 'views for the authorized donor, advisor, charity' of SOC evidence.
impact: Not a requirement: nothing distinguishes identity/fraud from vendor assurance; template text introduces nonsense scope.
proposed_resolution: Rewrite each as one outcome statement with its own acceptance; remove template persona lists where irrelevant.

title: IVR channel lacks demand evidence; numeric references are the durable value
description: REQ-X-025 specifies an IVR integration that is read-only, requires strong caller authentication and recordings review. Landscape evidence shows only 3 of 20 top sponsors publish phone hours and none publish service levels; there is no evidence donors ask for IVR self-service. Digit-only references are independently valuable for phone/mail support, check memos and recipient reconciliation. TVF-156 (accessible phone fallback vs step-up) remains open.
impact: Telephony vendor, authentication and privacy work for a channel of unproven use.
proposed_resolution: Keep the numeric reference requirement (split out); defer the IVR channel behind demand evidence and an approved assisted-channel assurance model (TVR-SEC-007).

title: White-label and dynamic terminology lack a locked legal-term list and channel consent rules
description: REQ-X-030 lets client labels differ from canonical terminology 'but cannot alter financial ... semantics' without defining which terms are locked (e.g. 'grant recommendation' must not become 'donation' or 'gift to charity'; sponsor legal name in disclosures). SMS is in scope without consent/opt-in requirements. Landscape research notes a white-label portal licensed to a sponsor may be a regulated platform type under California charitable platform rules.
impact: Misleading donor communications about who controls assets; regulatory exposure for the platform operator.
proposed_resolution: Add a protected-term registry (term, locked meaning, permitted synonyms) enforced at Brand Kit publication; add SMS consent requirements; needs counsel on TCPA and California Gov. Code 12599.9 platform classification.

title: No canonical notification event catalog
description: Notifications are required in six places but nothing lists notification events with class (mandatory legal/security, transactional, service, optional), channel, consent basis, whether a sponsor may disable it, deduplication key and quiet-hours rules.
impact: Mandatory notices can be disabled by preference; duplicate outreach (AIN-030) cannot be tested.
proposed_resolution: Gap requirement UNB-RCN-PLT-002.

title: API standard lists topics but defines no concrete conventions
description: UNB-API-STD-001..006 require idempotency, error codes, versioning, rate limits and deprecation but define no error model, idempotency-key scope and retention window, version scheme, pagination or concurrency token format; REQ-X-051 then introduces a second contract layer.
impact: Each component invents conventions; agents and partners cannot rely on uniform semantics.
proposed_resolution: Add one API convention document as a requirement: RFC 9457 problem details, Idempotency-Key header semantics (scope per caller+operation, retention >= provider dedup window), ETag/If-Match concurrency, URL or media-type major versioning, cursor pagination; REQ-X-051 metadata embedded as schema extensions.

title: Assistance Orchestrator context retrieval is not bound to the caller principal
description: UNB-AI-STD-001 requires agents to use the same governed APIs as humans, but REQ-X-053's in-process Context Broker and Safe Tool Gateway are not required to execute reads under the end user's principal and tenant binding; UNB-TEN-009 lists prompt construction as a tenant surface but no requirement forbids a service identity read.
impact: Prompt context could include data the user cannot see, leaking it through generated explanations.
proposed_resolution: Require every context read for an assistance session to execute through the public query layer with the initiating principal's VerifiedTenantContext, and log retrieved resource IDs.

title: Tenant selection for multi-partner users is not specified
description: UNB-TEN-004 forbids client-supplied tenant hints, yet advisors and sponsor staff may hold roles across partners (UNB-TEN-020) and INT-001 requires a global context selector. The rule for a user choosing among entitled tenants is missing.
impact: Implementers either disallow multi-partner users or accept unverified hints.
proposed_resolution: Allow the client to send an opaque tenant selection only from the server-issued entitlement list; the broker revalidates membership on every request and binds it to the session token.

title: UNB-UX-007 is untestable
description: 'Avoid exposing internal EF tool names ... unless genuinely relevant' has no test oracle.
impact: Cannot be verified.
proposed_resolution: Replace with a forbidden-term list checked in UI string catalogs and a content review step.

title: No owner for executing adversarial scenarios; Dokimos is a code-quality system
description: Mission text expects validation 'against Praxis and Dokimos governance' and scenario suites are written for execution, but Dokimos is documented as longitudinal code-quality measurement, not a scenario or simulation harness. No requirement names the component that executes DKS/ADV scenarios with deterministic mocks.
impact: Scenario suites may have no runner.
proposed_resolution: Name a scenario-harness component (F# test project with deterministic provider mocks) and let Dokimos record its results as quality evidence.

title: Duplicate: embedded widget security restated five times while TVR-WID items stay open
description: Embed safety is restated in AIN-029, INT-015, ADM-037, MON-022 and REQ-X-050 without the concrete limits recorded earlier (authority-revision propagation window TVF-015, transactional step-up TVF-136).
impact: Restatement creates an impression of coverage while the measurable parts are still open.
proposed_resolution: One embedded-widget security requirement incorporating TVR-WID-001..006 values.

title: 180-day charity revalidation is stated as a platform minimum although its only source calls it an unvalidated sponsor policy proposal
description: REQ-X-007 says 'reverify at least every 180 days'. REQ-X-018 layer L2 and gate G03 turn it into a platform-wide floor that sponsors cannot change (ADV-053), and CROSS-REQUIREMENT-CONSISTENCY section 5 calls it 'the approved 180-day limit'. The daf-landscape source record says it is 'a sponsor-proposed maximum comprehensive review interval, not a universal legal safe harbor', makes it 'configurable ... per sponsor and charity class' (CA-180-01) and says 'Do not treat the 180-day interval as a statutory rule'. The owner-decision register has no entry approving 180 days. No statute or regulation reviewed sets a revalidation interval. The vendor evidence (Vanguard Charitable citing Rev. Proc. 2011-33, batch-2a line 12) points to reliance on IRS status at the time of the grant, not to a periodic cycle. Counsel must confirm this.
impact: An unvalidated policy number is coded as a legal or platform invariant. If counsel picks another interval, or a per-fact cadence, every gate, state machine (TX-27), dashboard and metric built around 180 days has to be reworked. Sponsors may also wrongly think the platform has met a legal duty.
proposed_resolution: Classify the interval as platform compliance policy (authority type: policy, not statute). Make it a governed configuration parameter, CommonVerificationMaxAge, defined per evidence fact type, with an owner (CRCO plus GC), an effective date and a legal-basis note. Sponsors may set a stricter value only for their own grants. Until counsel approves a value, record 180 days as a proposed default. Keep execution-time critical checks (REQ-X-018) as the control that does not depend on the cycle.

title: One universal 180-day validity contradicts the rule that freshness is fact-, rail- and jurisdiction-specific
description: POLICY-PRECEDENCE line 124 says 'Cache TTL is fact/rail/jurisdiction-specific, never invented as a universal number'. UNB-RULE-015 requires freshness thresholds 'by jurisdiction and risk', and UNB-KNOW-025 rejects 'one global refresh cadence'. The same document's L2 row and gate G03 ('current evidence (<=180 days)') and TYPED-DECISION contract 1 ('Verification validity is no longer than 180 days') still apply one number to every fact: IRS status, state registration, officer data, sanctions and destination.
impact: The two rules cannot both be implemented. Some facts would be refreshed too often (static identity) and others too rarely (revocation and sanctions rely on separate monitoring that is not tied to the 180 days).
proposed_resolution: Replace the single validity with a typed freshness table: fact type, maximum age, monitoring source, execution-time recheck (yes or no) and owner. Then 180 days becomes, at most, the age limit for the 'comprehensive review' bundle.

title: Calendar expiry of vetting is modelled as a blocking hold rather than an automatic refresh
description: TX-27 moves a charity from CurrentEvidence to ExpiredOrAdverseHeld on 'Scheduled 180-day trigger or material adverse event' and 'Blocks affected unexecuted grants'. TX-18 sends recurring occurrences to a held case on 'Expired vetting'. These rows treat staleness the same as adverse evidence. The daf-landscape record requires a proactive refresh before expiry (CA-180-02) and automatic renewal with no operator touch (CA-180-06 and CA-180-08).
impact: Every charity reaching day 180 with no adverse change creates grant holds and queue items. This causes donor-visible delays and manual work for exactly the routine cases the program wants to automate.
proposed_resolution: Separate the states ReverificationDue, RefreshInProgress, Expired and HeldAdverse. Start a deterministic refresh at a configurable lead time. Hold grants only when evidence has passed its maximum age and the refresh failed or found adverse facts. Never move straight from 'due' to the adverse state.

title: 'Comprehensive revalidation' has no defined content
description: No requirement lists which facts the 180-day review re-verifies, which are covered by continuous monitoring, and which are checked at execution. Decision-inventory row SCV-03 uses the generic template text shared by most rows ('Apply versioned, sponsor-authorized eligibility, state, timing, deduplication and safety rules').
impact: The review cannot be tested, and coverage gaps between the three check layers cannot be found.
proposed_resolution: Define a ReverificationBundle contract: list the facts, the source per fact, pass criteria and the result type. Add acceptance tests for each fact.

title: No requirement defines the recipient classes that make a DAF distribution taxable
description: UNB-GRANT-023 allows 'other permitted recipients', and UNB-CHAR-020 lists 'private foundation and supporting organization considerations' without rules. None of the canonical requirements (REQ-X-007, REQ-X-018 gate G05/G06) blocks or routes: distributions to natural persons; distributions for a purpose outside IRC 170(c)(2)(B); recipients that need expenditure responsibility (for example private non-operating foundations, foreign organizations without an equivalency determination, and non-charities); and disqualified supporting organizations (Type III non-functionally integrated, and Type I/II where a donor or advisor controls a supported organization). The research layer recorded this (TVCTL-14, TVF-172, TVF-044) but no requirement adopted it. Authority type: statute (IRC 4966(c), 4966(d)(4)). The research marks the detail as unverified, so counsel must confirm it, including the effect of the 2023 proposed regulations REG-142338-07, which are not final.
impact: The routine straight-through path could make a taxable distribution, with excise tax on the sponsor and on any manager who knowingly agrees. This is the main legal risk in automated grant approval.
proposed_resolution: Add a RecipientClass taxonomy and a deterministic TaxableDistributionGate (see UNB-RCN-GRT-001). Each class maps to one of: route permitted, ER route required, prohibited, or counsel review. Classification uses IRS subsection, foundation code and supporting-organization type, plus a donor/advisor control test against the related-party graph. Classification never comes from AI.

title: No requirement blocks payments that benefit a donor, advisor or related person (IRC 4958(c)(2))
description: TVF-175 (open) records that no payee block exists for grants, loans, compensation or similar payments to donors, advisors or related persons. REQ-X-005 checks that the destination belongs to the intended charity, not whether the payee or the economic beneficiary is a related party. UNB-GRANT-011 only asks to 'evaluate' conflicts. Daf-landscape WL-10 shows the benefits involved (reimbursement, tuition, travel). Authority type: statute (4958(c)(2)). Counsel must confirm scope, including what counts as a related person and how fees paid to an advisor's firm are treated.
impact: Automatic excess-benefit treatment, and an irreversible payment.
proposed_resolution: Add UNB-RCN-GRT-002: a deterministic gate that compares the payee legal entity, destination owner and declared beneficiaries with the related-party registry. The result is a nonwaivable hold routed to counsel.

title: Gate G05 treats every pledge as prohibited, which contradicts IRS reliance guidance and real differences between sponsors
description: G05 requires 'no prohibited benefit, pledge, purchase'. Notice 2017-73 section 4 (IRS reliance guidance under section 7, not a regulation, and not superseded as of 2026-11-19 according to the daf-landscape evidence) describes conditions under which a DAF distribution linked to a pledge is not a more-than-incidental benefit under 4967. Top sponsors differ: AEF follows the notice, Fidelity allows only non-binding pledges, and DAFgiving360, Vanguard and others bar binding pledges. The daf-landscape record WL-09 says not to treat pledges as universally prohibited.
impact: A global hard stop on pledges is stricter than the guidance and blocks sponsors that rely on the notice. The opposite reading (no pledge rule) would be unsafe. This is a precedence question (L0 or L3) that has not been decided.
proposed_resolution: Move pledge handling from the global G05 to a sponsor L3 policy with values Prohibited, NonBindingOnly or Notice2017-73Conditions. The baseline is approved by counsel. If a sponsor chooses Notice2017-73Conditions, enforce all three conditions deterministically, including the remittance suppression in UNB-RCN-GRT-009.

title: Remittance and external-ID features can break the Notice 2017-73 condition that the sponsor must not mention a pledge
description: REQ-X-077 requires 'structured remittance metadata ... grant purpose' and a sponsor/provider external-ID crosswalk. REQ-X-063 lets external apps submit 'permitted metadata' and an origin reference, and DR-GR-08 allows donor-supplied external IDs. A recipient CRM pledge ID, or purpose text such as 'pledge payment', could flow into the sponsor's check memo, ACH addenda or remittance advice. The sponsor would then be 'making reference' to the pledge, which breaks condition 1 of Notice 2017-73 section 4.
impact: This could expose donors or managers to 4967 tax on grants the sponsor meant to keep inside the notice's conditions. The flow is automated, so no human would see it.
proposed_resolution: Classify outbound remittance fields as sponsor statements. Apply a deterministic filter that drops pledge identifiers and pledge vocabulary from sponsor-issued remittance when sponsor policy relies on the notice. Keep the inbound attribution internally as evidence only. Counsel must validate the filter.

title: The rules for capturing donor affirmations were never carried into the requirements
description: The daf-landscape record defines how affirmations must be captured: an explicit affirmative action with no pre-checked boxes (WL-06); evidence bound to the exact disclosure version hash, actor, channel and idempotency key (WL-07); renewal after material edits (WL-12); a bounded standing affirmation for recurring schedules (WL-13); server-side enforcement for widgets (WL-14); and separate affirmations for grants, debits and fees (WL-21). No UNB requirement covers this. Only TX-10 ('with required affirmation'), REQ-X-063 ('prohibited benefit affirmation') and G05 ('valid donor affirmation') mention affirmations, and none says what makes one valid.
impact: G05 and TX-10 cannot be tested. A widget or API could submit a grant without real affirmation evidence. Recurring grants could keep running on an affirmation made before the policy changed.
proposed_resolution: Adopt UNB-RCN-GRT-010, an AffirmationEvidence contract that G05 and TX-10 reference.

evidence: requirements/grants/END-TO-END-GRANT-LIFECYCLE-AND-OPERATING-MODEL.md:42;requirements/grants/END-TO-END-GRANT-LIFECYCLE-AND-OPERATING-MODEL.md:18;research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/19-questions/PROPOSED-CANONICAL-REQUIREMENTS-AND-ACCEPTANCE-2026-11-22.md:94;research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/19-questions/TRANSACTION-STATE-TRANSITION-MATRIX-2026-11-23.csv:19;requirements/grants/END-TO-END-GRANT-LIFECYCLE-AND-OPERATING-MODEL.md:81;research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/16-registers/findings.csv:13;research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/16-registers/findings.csv:84;research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/16-registers/findings.csv:87;daf-landscape:docs/automated-charity-assurance-180-day-decision-record-v0.1.md (test 'Recurring grant due after eligibility loss');daf-landscape:docs/grant-scheduling-fulfillment-fees-decision-record-v0.1.md (DR-GR-02, DR-GR-05, DR-GR-06)
title: What happens to a recurring occurrence held after an eligibility change is not specified
description: UNB-GRANT-027 only says 'Handle recurring grants when charity eligibility ... changes'. REQ-X-008 and TX-18 recheck each instance and hold it. Nothing says: whether a held occurrence is skipped or deferred, and how long it may stay held; whether it is paid in addition to the next occurrence once the charity is cleared (a catch-up double payment); when repeated holds suspend the schedule; who is notified; and whether the standing affirmation must be renewed. TVF-012, TVF-095 and TVF-098 are open, and no requirement resolves them.
impact: The result is either silent loss of donor intent or an unexpected catch-up payment. The answer will be improvised in operations.
proposed_resolution: Adopt UNB-RCN-GRT-004. By default a held occurrence is skipped once a configurable hold window expires, with no automatic catch-up. Each occurrence has its own idempotency key (schedule version plus period). After a configurable number of consecutive adverse holds the schedule is suspended. The donor is notified. Default values need a sponsor policy decision.

title: There are six incompatible payment-state vocabularies, and TX-13 merges Unknown with Accepted
description: The payment-state vocabularies are: UNB-GRANT-022 (prepared...reconciled); UNB-PAY-009 (pending/approved/sent/settled/failed/returned); the TYPED-DECISION contract 3 outputs (a linear Prepared...FinalityConfirmed); the POLICY-PRECEDENCE payment-release outcomes; the financial-core lifecycle; and REQ-X-083's six orthogonal dimensions, which say 'Do not collapse ... into a single ordered status'. TX-13's target state 'ProviderUnknownOrAccepted' joins exactly the two states that REQ-X-083 and REQ-X-004 must keep apart.
impact: Implementers cannot tell which model is authoritative. Merging Unknown with Accepted removes the distinction that blocks blind retries.
proposed_resolution: Declare REQ-X-083 the canonical model. Mark UNB-GRANT-022, UNB-PAY-001 and UNB-PAY-009 as superseded and TYPED-DECISION contract 3 as derived. Split TX-13 into the transitions DispatchOutcomeUnknown and Acknowledged. Publish one mapping from the dimensions to UI labels.

title: Uncashed, stale-dated, voided and escheated checks have no lifecycle
description: UNB-PAY-006 asks only to support 'escheat/unclaimed property applicability'. The REQ-X-083 dimensions have no state for outstanding or aged checks, for a void after aging, or for unclaimed-property reporting or remittance, and they do not say what happens to the grant reservation or to fund capacity. CTL-044 (aging and escheat workflow, Controller) exists in conversion wave 04 but no grant or payment requirement links to it. TVF-023, TVF-088, TVF-184 and TVF-199 remain open. Authority types: state unclaimed-property statutes (jurisdiction-specific), the sponsor's bank contract, and sponsor policy. Counsel must decide whether a voided grant may go back to the DAF or to another charity, or must be escheated.
impact: Grants show as issued for years. The reservation is stuck or consumed while the charity never receives the funds. Late presentment after a void can cause a double payment, and unclaimed-property filing duties can be missed.
proposed_resolution: Adopt UNB-RCN-GRT-005: the states Outstanding, AgedOutreach, StaleDated, VoidRequested, VoidConfirmed and UnclaimedPropertyReportable. Each state has a ledger effect and a reissue chain, and the aging thresholds are configuration owned by the Controller.

title: A true sanctions match has no Blocked outcome, so the money would follow return or retry paths
description: The 'Provider knowledge' and 'Settlement evidence' dimensions in REQ-X-083 have no Blocked or Rejected-by-sanctions value. No ledger state exists for blocked property, and nothing covers a payment blocked by an intermediary bank. TVF-171 and TVF-210 are open and REQ-X-083 does not resolve them. Authority type: OFAC regulations, including the blocked-property and rejected-transaction reporting duties in 31 CFR Part 501. Counsel must confirm which duties apply to the sponsor, to its bank, or to both.
impact: Blocked funds could be treated as returned and re-granted, released back to the fund, or reissued. Each of these could be a sanctions violation, and the required reports would not be made.
proposed_resolution: Add Blocked to the provider-knowledge and settlement dimensions and add a BlockedProperty ledger classification. Release is allowed only by license evidence and independent compliance authority (UNB-RCN-GRT-006). There is no retry, reissue or capacity restoration while blocked.

title: The sanctions screening scope is undefined: which subjects, which lists, when, and what rescreens in-flight items
description: The requirements say 'check current sanctions ... at execution' (REQ-X-007) and 'OFAC and other legally applicable ... lists' (UNB-EXT-004). They do not say which parties are screened: recipient legal entity, fiscal sponsor, project, named officers, payee bank, intermediary banks, beneficiary country, donor or advisor. They do not say which lists are used, whether ownership aggregation applies, whether a list update rescreens approved but unpaid grants, or what counts as a match. UNB-RULE-014 refers to an undefined 'required threshold'. TVF-027 and TVF-048 are open.
impact: The screening could not be shown to be adequate, false-positive handling (OD-02) has no subject to apply to, and cross-border payments are particularly exposed.
proposed_resolution: Adopt UNB-RCN-GRT-007, a ScreeningScope matrix (subject x list x trigger x threshold owner) approved by counsel. A list update rescreens every unreleased payment chain.

title: Atomic 'currency reservation' does not say how to reserve grants that are funded by selling investments
description: REQ-X-002 and TX-11 reserve currency atomically against net capacity at approval. UNB-GFUND-011 and UNB-GFUND-021 fund many grants by redeeming pool units or positions after approval, and GF-ADR-005 (when reservations are made and released) is still open. If the reservation is a dollar amount but the source is units, a fall in NAV between approval and redemption leaves the approved grant underfunded. That breaks the 'no overcommitment' acceptance in REQ-X-002, and GEX-T02/EXC-03 then holds an already approved grant.
impact: Approved grants can become unpayable, or other grants could be paid from the shortfall. The REQ-X-002 guarantee only holds for cash-funded grants.
proposed_resolution: Define the reservation unit for each funding source: cash amount, units with a valuation haircut, or a sale before approval. Add an ApprovedPendingLiquidity state that creates no external commitment, and state the shortfall rule (reduce, top up from a waterfall, or hold). The CFO must decide.

title: The result of a percentage grant depends on the order in which concurrent grants and reservations are processed
description: UNB-GFUND-002 allows 'eligible available-to-recommend balance' as the base. Nothing says whether that base is measured before or after pending reservations, other percentage grants made at the same moment, fee accruals or the grant's own reservation. Two 50% grants created together could total 100% or 75% depending on the order of evaluation.
impact: Grant amounts would not be deterministic and could not be replayed (UNB-GRANT-038).
proposed_resolution: Define the base as a snapshot at a pinned valuation point that excludes this grant's own reservation and includes all reservations committed earlier. Concurrent percentage grants serialise at the reservation boundary, and each is recalculated if its snapshot changed.

title: There is no defined way for an Unknown payment to ever be resolved
description: REQ-X-004 blocks resubmission 'until contractually sufficient independently controlled evidence proves non-receipt'. TVF-024 (open) records that most rails cannot prove non-receipt. REQ-X-083 adds no aging, query protocol, escalation, or evidence combination (for example provider status query, bank statement absence after the rail's settlement window, recipient confirmation, and a written provider attestation) that would allow resolution. Nothing makes it eventually terminal.
impact: Grants can stay reserved and unpaid with no end date, causing donor complaints and capacity lock-up. Staff will improvise, which is the condition that leads to duplicate payments.
proposed_resolution: Adopt UNB-RCN-GRT-008: an Unknown resolution protocol with rail-specific evidence combinations, an aging schedule, independent approval to declare NotReceived, and a mandatory linked reissue chain. Treasury and the provider contract owners set the thresholds.

title: The destination-proof standard does not name any qualifying evidence, so it may make every automated payment impossible
description: REQ-X-005 requires independently verifiable proof of charity control and of the execution destination, and rejects provider self-attestation. Under the E-class model, account-ownership validation services and provider feeds are E3 ('cannot alone establish payment destination'). No requirement names the evidence that does qualify for each rail: a bank-originated account-owner match, a prenote or micro-deposit, an independent callback to a contact found from a separate source, or a positive-pay reconciled check image. Paper checks have no destination-control proof defined at all.
impact: If nothing qualifies, every payment falls to manual review, which defeats rules-first STP (REQ-X-017). If teams invent their own definition of what qualifies, the control is uneven.
proposed_resolution: Publish a per-rail DestinationEvidence table, owned by Treasury, that classifies named evidence types into E-classes and gives the minimum combination for automated release. Treat it as configuration with independent publication.

title: ACH Notification of Change handling is unspecified and may conflict with pinned, independently verified destinations
description: REQ-X-083 invariant 2 pins the payee destination version, and REQ-X-005/TX-19 require independent verification before a destination changes. ACH network rules require the originator to apply correction information from a Notification of Change within a set time. The current NACHA Operating Rules text and deadline must be confirmed; authority type: private network rule enforced by contract. No requirement says whether an NOC is a destination change, whether it counts as independent bank-originated evidence, or whether payments are held until it is verified.
impact: If the requirements are followed literally, they may breach network rules, or an NOC could become an unverified way to redirect payments.
proposed_resolution: Classify NOC as RDFI-originated E1 evidence, which creates a new destination version through TX-19 using an expedited verification path. Hold further entries to that destination until the new version is effective. Treasury and counsel must confirm against the current rules.

title: The check rail proof row leaves out the positive-pay issue and void files
description: The REQ-X-083 check row lists 'verified mailing address, check number, authorized print/release', but has no positive-pay issue file or void file, even though UNB-GAP-009 names positive pay. Bank-portal positive-pay decisions are payment decisions with no independent control (TVF-232).
impact: Altered or counterfeit checks could clear, and a voided check could still be honored.
proposed_resolution: Add positive-pay issue and void file submission and acknowledgment as required evidence for the transitions to Dispatch=SentWithRequestId and VoidConfirmed. Add bank-portal exception decisions to the payment authority model.

title: Callback deduplication uses only providerEventId, with no authentication or semantic rule
description: RecordProviderEvidence deduplicates on providerEventId. Providers can send the same fact under new event IDs (for example on redelivery after migration), or several events that mean the same state. REQ-X-083 does not require verifying the callback's signature or source, even though REQ-X-063 requires signed callbacks. PAY-09 sends every contradiction to an exception case.
impact: Semantic duplicates can produce two accounting effects, and forged callbacks could move the settlement state.
proposed_resolution: Make the deduplication key (provider, providerEventId) plus a semantic key (paymentId, dimension, target state, amount, currency, effectiveAt). Require authenticated callbacks (signature or mTLS) before evidence is recorded. Resolve known benign orderings deterministically, for example Acknowledged arriving after Executed.

title: Several exception classes always send work to a human even when a rule could settle it
description: EXC-01 always says 'request compliance decision' for eligibility drift, EXC-02 always requires steward review, and PAY-09 always opens a case. Under REQ-X-017, an authoritative revocation should simply block, a source refresh that confirms the status is unchanged should release the hold automatically, and an exact match on EIN plus jurisdiction plus legal name should resolve identity. These exceptions predate REQ-X-017 and were never reconciled with it.
impact: Queues grow with routine cases, and the STP metrics in REQ-X-017 cannot be met.
proposed_resolution: Rewrite EXC-01, EXC-02 and PAY-09 as: deterministic resolution table first, bounded evidence retrieval second, human only for the cases left over. Reason codes must show which tier resolved each case.

title: The grant requirements assume a human approves grants and grant modifications; REQ-X-017 assumes rules approve routine cases
description: UNB-GRANT-012 routes 'human approvals according to role, amount, risk...' and UNB-GRANT-048 'Require[s] human approval of material grant modifications after sponsor approval'. REQ-X-017 says Tier 1 deterministic policy resolves routine approvals 'without AI or human intervention'. REQ-X-001 says a material change invalidates approval, and that a rule may re-approve. Industry evidence puts non-standard grants at about 2.5 to 3% of dollars at large national sponsors. TVC-003 and OD-01 are still open and do not mention UNB-GRANT-012 or UNB-GRANT-048.
impact: Unclear whether straight-through approval is allowed at all, and a large manual approval queue if the older text wins.
proposed_resolution: Restate UNB-GRANT-012 and UNB-GRANT-048 as: approval authority is either board-delegated policy (once OD-01 is validated) or an independent human. A material modification invalidates approval and is re-decided by the same routing. Keep OD-01 as the gate.

title: Sponsor eligibility overrides (UNB-CHAR-023) conflict with the rule that sponsors cannot lower common vetting
description: UNB-CHAR-023 allows sponsor-specific overrides within lawful policy, with independent review. REQ-X-018 layer L2 and ADV-053 forbid any sponsor from weakening common vetting. Typical case: the common standard returns InsufficientEvidence for a church that is not in the IRS files, and the sponsor holds its own evidence.
impact: Implementers must pick one rule. Either sponsors can bypass the common standard, or legitimate alternate-evidence grants are blocked.
proposed_resolution: See RCC-GRT-003: allow sponsor-supplied evidence to be added to the common record through the alternate-verification path (UNB-RCN-GRT-013). Never allow a sponsor to override a common adverse or Ineligible result.

title: Spreading adverse findings to every sponsor conflicts with keeping sponsor investigations confidential
description: REQ-X-007 says 'Adverse findings propagate to all affected sponsors'. UNB-CHAR-036, UNB-EXT-033, CHAR-T10 and KNOW-T10 keep sponsor investigations private, and UNB-CHAR-037 requires an explicit rule on whether sponsor-derived intelligence may improve the common registry. UNB-EXT-015 requires due process and anti-defamation safeguards. Nothing defines who may turn a single sponsor's private finding into a global hold, what evidence that needs, or what other sponsors see.
impact: A single sponsor could hold a charity for every sponsor based on unverified private allegations, creating defamation exposure. Or sponsors could keep material adverse facts hidden.
proposed_resolution: See RCC-GRT-004. Propagate only a typed status (HeldAdverse with a reason category), never the private evidence. A global hold requires E0 or E1 evidence or independent compliance authority. Other sponsors see the reason class and the date, not the source.

title: 'Eligibility' means two different things and has five different state vocabularies
description: UNB-CHAR-019 defines eligibility per sponsor, program, purpose, geography, amount and date, with results Eligible/Ineligible/NeedsReview/InsufficientEvidence (UNB-CHAR-021). The RULE disposition is ProceedToSponsorApproval/HoldForEvidence/HoldForReview/Block/Expired. TYPED-DECISION contract 1 uses EligibleCommon/IneligibleCommon/HoldEvidence/HoldAdverse/DisputedIdentity/VerificationExpired, POLICY-PRECEDENCE uses HeldForEvidence/HeldForAdverse, and daf-landscape uses NotAssessed...Expired. REQ-X-007 uses 'vetting' for the common status but the charity files call that eligibility.
impact: Inconsistent states across components lead to mismapped holds, for example a sponsor denial being written to the global record.
proposed_resolution: Use two terms: CommonVerificationStatus (global, one enumeration) and GrantEligibilityDecision (sponsor-scoped, one enumeration). Retire the other names and publish a crosswalk.

title: Append-only history, temporal queries and replay are assigned to Strata, which is a schema-migration tool
description: The grant lifecycle text says 'Strata persistence required' and 'Strata interfaces'. UNB-GEX-002, UNB-CHAR-040 ('Strata-backed immutable observations ... temporal queries, source replay') and UNB-KNOW-014 assign event-store, ledger and bitemporal capabilities to Strata. kemiller2002/strata is a pilot-stage declarative PostgreSQL schema management tool and provides none of these.
impact: The requirements depend on a capability that does not exist. Ordering, replay and immutability guarantees would have no owner.
proposed_resolution: Restate these as technology-neutral capability requirements: append-only journal tables, bitemporal columns, and replay from the outbox, implemented in the authoritative PostgreSQL core. Limit Strata to schema definition and migration, subject to its own verification.

title: The 60-event grant catalog has no events for Unknown, void, recall, reissue, blocked, escheat, affirmation or held occurrences
description: GR-EVT-042..050 cover drafted, approved, simulated, submission recorded, acknowledged, settlement evidence, return and reconciliation. They have no events for the REQ-X-083 commands (DispatchOutcomeUnknown, RequestVoidOrRecall, VoidConfirmed, ReissuePayment), nor for Blocked, UnclaimedPropertyReported, AffirmationRecorded, OccurrenceHeld or OccurrenceSkipped, GrantDeclinedByRecipient, or a grant cancellation separate from GR-EVT-028 commitment reversal.
impact: Implementers will add events ad hoc and the catalog's 'canonical' claim will not hold.
proposed_resolution: Regenerate the catalog from the REQ-X-083 commands and the TX matrix, with one event per authoritative transition.

title: Every event must carry sponsor, partner and DAF IDs, which common charity-registry events do not have
description: The event envelope requires 'sponsorId, partnerId, legalEntityId, DAFId' on every event. GR-EVT-011 CharityEvidenceChanged and common adverse holds are platform-wide under REQ-X-007, so they would need a fake sponsor ID or a copy per sponsor, which contradicts 'no duplicate routine vetting'.
impact: Either duplicated global events or invalid envelopes.
proposed_resolution: Define envelope scope as Platform | Sponsor | Fund. Platform-scoped events carry no tenant IDs, and the authorization rules for each scope are stated explicitly.

title: Duplicate: bank-detail change control is defined six times at different strengths
description: Bank-detail change control is defined in UNB-GRANT-026, UNB-GEX-018 ('dual control per policy'), UNB-CHAR-032, UNB-PAY-005, REQ-X-005 ('independent authorization without self-approval ... provider self-attestation insufficient') and TX-19. The weaker wordings ('per policy') could be read as allowing single control.
impact: Inconsistent implementation, and the weakest wording becomes the de facto standard.
proposed_resolution: Make REQ-X-005 (refined as RR-REQ-X-005-r1) canonical and mark the others as refined-by references.

title: Duplicate: execution-time rechecks are stated seven times, some of them optional
description: UNB-GRANT-009 rechecks 'at policy-defined stages', and UNB-RULE-015 says 'where required'. REQ-X-018 and REQ-X-019 make execution-time rechecks mandatory. The optional wordings could be configured off.
impact: A sponsor policy could legitimately skip the recheck at release.
proposed_resolution: Make the REQ-X-018 execution-time recheck canonical and nonconfigurable for sanctions, common status, holds and destination, and supersede the optional wordings.

title: The canonical REQ-X-058..077 entries are template text and their detail files list cases without expected results
description: REQ-X-065, REQ-X-069 and REQ-X-077 have identical normative text ('Extend the one Unbound component monolith ... See the dedicated ... specification'). The detail files list 'Synthetic cases' (for example 'Restricted jurisdiction, stale determination ... sanctioned intermediary') with no expected state. Decision-inventory rows G-02, G-05 and SCV-03 repeat the same template.
impact: None of these can be tested or traced. They count as coverage without saying anything.
proposed_resolution: Replace each with a normative statement plus given/when/then acceptance, using the refinement records here for the highest-risk items.

title: The base grant and charity requirements have no RFC 2119 keywords and their scenarios are not traced to IDs
description: Heuristic counts: UNB-GRANT has 0 of 48 with an RFC 2119 keyword and 2 of 48 with an acceptance signal; UNB-GEX 0/40 and 3/40; UNB-RULE 0/32 and 1/32; UNB-CHAR 5/42 and 2/42. Many requirements say only 'Support X' or 'Handle X'. The scenario sets GRANT-T*, GEX-T*, CHAR-T* and RULE-T* do not cite the requirement IDs they test.
impact: Requirements cannot be verified and there is no traceability from requirement to test.
proposed_resolution: Convert to MUST/SHOULD statements, and add a requirement-ID column to each scenario list.

title: International grants lack the equivalency-determination and expenditure-responsibility obligations, and ownership of the decision is contradictory
description: REQ-X-065 item 2 says only 'Equivalency determination and expenditure responsibility routes when applicable'. It does not cover the pre-grant inquiry, written agreement terms, reporting and follow-up, Form 990/Schedule D reporting inputs, the basis for good-faith reliance on an equivalency determination, its expiry, or whether one determination can be reused across sponsors. REQ-X-065 says 'Sponsor/legal counsel owns eligibility', while L2 makes eligibility platform-wide. TVCTL-12 and TVF-044 are open. Authority types: statute (4945(h) through 4966(c)) and Treasury regulations on good-faith determinations. Counsel must confirm application to DAFs.
impact: ER grants could be paid without their obligations being tracked, causing taxable distributions. Platform vetting could be wrongly relied on for foreign grants.
proposed_resolution: Adopt UNB-RCN-GRT-003 (ER obligation lifecycle). Mark foreign-recipient decisions as sponsor-scoped (L3) unless counsel approves a reliance agreement.

title: Nothing stops a charity from issuing the donor a deductible-gift receipt for a DAF grant
description: REQ-X-077 supports 'Recipient CRM matching, acknowledgement and corrected attribution', and REQ-X-063 checkout links donors to charity checkout flows. No requirement makes remittance carry a statement that the grant comes from the sponsoring organization and is not a deductible gift by the donor. Notice 2017-73 condition 3 depends on no one claiming a 170 deduction for the distribution. Authority type: best practice backed by IRS guidance. Counsel must confirm the wording.
impact: Donors may claim a second deduction, and sponsors relying on the pledge conditions are exposed.
proposed_resolution: Adopt UNB-RCN-GRT-011: a mandatory remittance statement and an acknowledgement contract that records the sponsor as legal donor.

title: Embedded checkout does not capture what is being bought, so ticket purchases cannot be detected
description: REQ-X-063's typed recommendation carries charity, amount, intent and metadata, but not the host page context (event ticket, table, auction, membership tier). INV-16 ('Ticket purchase disguised as donation') can therefore only rely on donor self-declaration, even though checkout on ticket pages is the most direct 4967 risk.
impact: Prohibited-benefit grants could pass straight through.
proposed_resolution: Adopt UNB-RCN-GRT-012: the host declares a checkout context type, the server rejects or routes to review when the context carries a benefit, and widget certification is required.

title: What happens to returned, refunded or declined grant money is undefined
description: UNB-GRANT-028 lists returns, refunds and declined grants. TX-15 says 'restore capacity only under policy'. Nothing says: whether funds go back to the originating fund; how a charity's later refund differs from a bank return; that no donor tax receipt is issued on re-credit; or that a charity can decline a grant before payment. TVF-078 (open) notes that NotReceived, Recalled and Voided have no grant transition.
impact: Funds could be misallocated, a contribution receipt could be wrongly issued, and grants could be left in limbo.
proposed_resolution: Adopt UNB-RCN-GRT-015. Accounting treatment needs CPA approval.

title: G03 has no defined alternate-evidence path for legitimate recipients that are not in the IRS files
description: UNB-CHAR-016 says absence from a dataset is not ineligibility. Daf-landscape evidence shows that many top DAF recipient EINs (government units, disregarded subsidiaries, churches, group-exemption subordinates) appear in no IRS bulk file. G03 requires E0/E1 'platform-standard vetted' evidence, and no requirement says which alternate evidence satisfies it for each entity type.
impact: False holds fall mostly on churches, schools and public universities, causing manual queues and fairness problems (batch-2c H5).
proposed_resolution: Adopt UNB-RCN-GRT-013: an entity-type evidence matrix approved by counsel (government unit, church, group subordinate, disregarded entity of a listed parent).

title: GRANT-T19 says a schedule 'survives donor death'; REQ-X-008 says future instructions are suspended
description: The scenario wording suggests the schedule keeps running. REQ-X-008 and DR-GR-06 suspend future instances until successor authority is verified.
impact: Ambiguous test oracle.
proposed_resolution: Reword GRANT-T19 as: 'schedule is suspended, not cancelled; resumes only under verified successor authority'.

title: Nothing says what to do when an adverse event arrives after a payment has been dispatched
description: REQ-X-020 says holds placed after submission 'cannot guarantee reversal'. No requirement says what must happen when a charity is revoked or sanctioned after a check is mailed or an ACH is sent but before settlement: attempt a stop or recall, notify the sponsor, open a case, decide the grant's disposition. The sanctions case is covered by the Blocked finding.
impact: Avoidable payments to entities found ineligible are not stopped.
proposed_resolution: Adopt UNB-RCN-GRT-016.

title: 180-day revalidation treated as the currency standard for charity status
description: The overlay treats evidence up to 180 days old as current and makes 180 days a platform norm sponsors cannot downgrade. Rev. Proc. 2018-32 reliance is assessed as of each grant date and requires the grantor to keep a copy of the third-party report (§8.01). No law sets 180 days.
impact: Grants to a charity revoked inside the window could be taxable distributions under §4966; shared evidence would not satisfy per-sponsor retention.
proposed_resolution: Adopt RR-REQ-X-007-r1: an IRS-status check at approval and at release, a per-sponsor snapshot, and 180 days as a sponsor-configurable deep-review interval.

title: Carried REG-001 row says grant approval cannot be vested in software
description: §4966 taxes a manager who knowingly agrees to a taxable distribution; it does not require human approval of each grant. Whether to delegate is a governance and state-law question. Already raised as TVC-003 and OD-01, but the carried row text remains uncorrected.
impact: Could either block a lawful automation model or be read as legal certainty in either direction.
proposed_resolution: Annotate the row as overstated; resolve through counsel Q1 and RCD-005.

title: Retention floor lacks authority-keyed classes (OFAC 10 years)
description: The 7-year floor correctly yields to longer obligations, but no record class names one. OFAC records require 10 years (31 CFR 501.601, effective 2025-03-21).
impact: Sanctions records could be offered for disposition early.
proposed_resolution: Adopt RR-REQ-X-036-r1.

title: Exclusive legal control cited to the wrong section
description: The wording comes from §170(f)(18)(B), the donor-acknowledgment rule, not §4966(d)(2). No requirement specifies acknowledgment content.
impact: Acknowledgments could omit the statement, which would cost donors their deduction (strict compliance).
proposed_resolution: Adopt RR-UNB-ACC-006-r1 with acknowledgment content.

title: Donor control of supporting organizations cannot be determined from IRS data
description: §4966(d)(4) makes grants to donor-controlled Type I/II/FI-III supporting organizations taxable without expenditure responsibility. TEOS/BMF cannot show control, and no requirement demands a certification.
impact: Taxable distributions through automated eligibility.
proposed_resolution: Add UNB-RCN-REG-002.

title: OFAC blocking and reporting duties are not specified
description: Requirements cover screening and holds but not the blocking of property, the 10-business-day blocked-property report or the annual report. Screening itself is a risk-based practice, not a mandated method.
impact: Non-compliance with 31 CFR 501.603/604 after a true match.
proposed_resolution: Add UNB-RCN-REG-003; label screening authority as best practice.

title: KYC/CIP applicability correctly left open; must not be imported as law
description: No BSA/CIP mandate applies to a charity paying its own grants. The answer may change if a for-profit administrator holds or moves funds.
impact: Over-engineering onboarding or mislabeling controls as legal duties.
proposed_resolution: Keep identity verification as a fraud and authorization control; counsel Q8.

title: Superseded Rev. Proc. 2011-33 cited in evidence
description: Rev. Proc. 2018-32 supersedes it, with the same substance.
impact: Stale citation propagates into requirements.
proposed_resolution: Cite Rev. Proc. 2018-32 in all new records.

title: No regulatory-change watch for pending DAF guidance
description: REG-142338-07 is still proposed, and the 2026–27 PGP lists §§4966/6033 DAF guidance. No requirement assigns monitoring or impact review.
impact: Requirements silently drift from law when guidance issues.
proposed_resolution: Add UNB-RCN-REG-001.

title: No excess-business-holdings computation
description: §4943(e) applies to DAFs, including holdings of donors and related persons. Complex-asset requirements do not compute it.
impact: Accepting closely held business interests could trigger §4943 taxes.
proposed_resolution: Adopt UNB-RCN-FIN-004 (consolidated; UNB-RCN-REG-004 withdrawn as duplicate).

title: Strata assigned capabilities it does not have
description: Strata v0.1.1 (pilot) is a declarative PostgreSQL schema-management CLI. It provides no append-only history, posting, temporal query, replay, projection or data integrity check.
impact: The persistence architecture is unimplementable as written; financial integrity would rest on a non-existent capability.
proposed_resolution: Adopt RR-UNB-PLAT-007-r1: an Unbound-owned Ledger/Event Store on managed PostgreSQL, with Strata as the schema-governance and drift layer.

title: Dynamic terminology has no owner
description: Forma excludes terminology by design (BRAND-012), and no Unbound requirement assigns it.
impact: Inconsistent sponsor vocabulary across channels; legally required phrases could be overridden.
proposed_resolution: Add UNB-RCN-ARC-002.

title: No contract source of truth or format
description: Versioned contracts are required, but no requirement names the format, the generation source or a breaking-change gate.
impact: Drift between code, documentation and AI-discoverable contracts.
proposed_resolution: Add UNB-RCN-ARC-001.

title: Protective emergency plane and outage intake add a second durable system
description: REQ-X-020/021 introduce an independently durable protective-only plane and nonauthoritative intake outside the monolith, without cost, ownership or failure-mode evidence that managed-database high availability is insufficient.
impact: Operational complexity contrary to the managed, modular-monolith direction.
proposed_resolution: Require an ADR showing the failure mode that managed HA plus a read-only degraded mode cannot handle before building a separate plane (RCD-012).

title: Donor-facing charity search is not specified
description: The first-party charity registry is specified for eligibility, but no requirement lets a donor or advisor find a charity by name, EIN, location or cause and see its eligibility before recommending. Every readable self-serve portal documents this (CAP-12).
impact: Recommendations arrive with ambiguous identities, which forces manual resolution downstream (TVF identity disputes).
proposed_resolution: Add UNB-RCN-PLT-014.
